title: The New Era of Respiratory Syncytial Virus Protection for Infants: A Mini Review of Current Tools for Immunoprophylaxis
abstract: ABSTRACT Aim This mini review describes the history of infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis and the latest advances in this area. It also reviews the efficacy, safety and impact of the recently introduced prophylactic strategies. Method This narrative review is based on a targeted review of published literature, with emphasis on pivotal clinical trials, regulatory documents and recent real‐world evidence. Results Three immunisation products for preventing RSV in infants have been approved since 2022. These are two long‐acting monoclonal antibodies, nirsevimab and clesrovimab, and a maternal RSV vaccine. The efficacy of these interventions has ranged from 49% to 76% against medically attended RSV‐associated lower respiratory tract infections and from 55% to 91% against hospitalisation due to RSV‐associated lower respiratory tract infection. The efficacy varied between the products and the duration of the follow‐up. Similar or higher effectiveness has been reported in post‐licensure, real‐world evidence studies. Overall, these interventions have been well tolerated, with favourable safety profiles. Conclusion The newly introduced long‐acting monoclonal antibodies and the maternal RSV vaccine have proved highly effective and have demonstrated reassuring safety. They have already been implemented in a number of countries and have substantially reduced the RSV burden in infants.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; Orthopneumovirus hominis, including RSV-A and RSV-B) immunoprophylaxis for infants, focusing on the central question of the efficacy, safety, and impact of recently introduced prophylactic strategies.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes published literature with emphasis on pivotal clinical trials, regulatory documents, and recent real-world evidence; eligibility criteria and selection methods are not explicitly reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Three immunoprophylaxis products for infants have been approved since 2022: two long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab and clesrovimab) and a maternal RSV vaccine, with efficacy ranging from 49% to 76% against medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections and 55% to 91% against hospitalization due to RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infection.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report heterogeneity in efficacy estimates by geographic region, socioeconomic status, or high-risk subgroups, nor does it address long-term safety beyond initial approval phases.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Post-licensure effectiveness studies should prioritize monitoring durability of protection, safety in preterm infants, and implementation strategies in low-resource settings to optimize global RSV burden reduction.

analysis.summary_en: This mini-review evaluates recent advances in infant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunoprophylaxis, focusing on two long-acting monoclonal antibodies (nirsevimab and clesrovimab) and a maternal RSV vaccine approved since 2022. Across pivotal trials and real-world evidence, efficacy against medically attended RSV-associated lower respiratory tract infections ranges from 49% to 76%, and against hospitalization from 55% to 91%, with favorable safety profiles. These interventions have been implemented in multiple countries and have substantially reduced infant RSV burden. Key gaps include limited data on long-term safety, durability of protection, and effectiveness across diverse populations and settings.

abstract_zh: 摘要 目的 这篇简短的综述介绍了婴儿 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 免疫预防的历史以及该领域的最新进展。它还回顾了最近引入的预防策略的有效性、安全性和影响。方法 本叙述性综述基于对已发表文献的有针对性的综述,重点是关键临床试验、监管文件和最新的现实世界证据。结果 自 2022 年以来,已有三种用于预防婴儿 RSV 的免疫产品获得批准。它们是两种长效单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗 和 clesrovimab,以及一种母体 RSV 疫苗。这些干预措施对就诊的 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染的疗效为 49% 至 76%,对因 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染而住院的疗效为 55% 至 91%。不同产品和随访时间的疗效各不相同。在获得许可后的真实世界证据研究中也报告了类似或更高的有效性。总体而言,这些干预措施的耐受性良好,且安全性良好。结论 新推出的长效单克隆抗体和母源RSV 疫苗已被证明具有高效性且安全性令人放心。这些措施已在许多国家实施,并大大减少了婴儿的呼吸道合胞病毒负担。

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这篇叙述性综述综合了已发表的文献,重点是关键的临床试验、监管文件和最近的现实世界证据;没有明确报告资格标准和选择方法。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 自 2022 年以来,已有三种婴儿免疫预防产品获得批准:两种长效单克隆抗体(尼塞韦单抗 和 clesrovimab)和一种母体 RSV 疫苗,对就诊的 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染的疗效为 49% 至 76%,对因 RSV 相关下呼吸道感染而住院的疗效为 55% 至 91%。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查没有报告按地理区域、社会经济状况或高风险亚组划分的疗效估计的异质性,也没有解决初始批准阶段之后的长期安全性。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 许可后有效性研究应优先监测保护的持久性、早产儿的安全性以及资源匮乏环境中的实施策略,以优化全球 RSV 负担减轻。

title: Maternal RSVpreF Vaccine Effectiveness Against Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Hospitalized Infants
abstract: IMPORTANCE: In February 2025, Australia introduced maternal vaccination with bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in the National Immunization Program for pregnant individuals from 28 weeks' gestation as the primary, year-round strategy to prevent RSV disease in infants 6 months of age or younger. OBJECTIVE: To estimate effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination during pregnancy against infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks' gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. EXPOSURE: Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks' gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 - adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. RESULTS: Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

Design, Setting, and Participants This retrospective case-control study with a test-negative design was conducted in 9 hospitals across Australia with year-round respiratory testing for acute respiratory illness (ARI) among infants born from 28 weeks’ gestation and hospitalized with ARI at 6 months of age or younger, March 1, 2025, through February 28, 2026. Data were analyzed March 2026 through May 2026. Exposure Maternal RSVpreF vaccination administered from 28 weeks’ gestation and 14 days or more before delivery. Main Outcomes and Measures Maternal RSVpreF effectiveness was evaluated against hospitalization for RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD, primary objective), severe RSV-LRTD, and RSV-ARI. Logistic regression with confounder adjustment was used to calculate vaccine effectiveness (VE) as (1 − adjusted odds ratio) × 100%. Results Of 1012 infants hospitalized with ARI, 655 had LRTD, with 114 of 386 case infants (30%) and 171 of 269 control infants (64%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers (median [IQR] gestational age at vaccination, 31 weeks [29-33]). Median (IQR) maternal age at delivery was 32 years (29-35). Median (IQR) age of infants hospitalized for LRTD was 52 days (30-89); 495 of 655 (76%) were aged 3 months or younger. VE against RSV-LRTD hospitalization was 77.8% (95% CI, 66.4%-85.3%) among infants from birth through 6 months of age, 80.2% (95% CI, 71.1%-86.5%) among infants from birth through 3 months of age, 86.3% (95% CI, 79.0%-91.1%) among infants from birth through 2 months of age, and 68.2% (95% CI, 42.2%-82.5%) among infants older than 2 months through 4 months of age. Comparable VE among infants aged 6 months or younger was observed for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%; 95% CI, 54.4%-91.6%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%; 95% CI, 70.4%-87.6%) hospitalization, with similar age-specific trends. VE was consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination, vaccination to delivery time interval, and proximal administration with other vaccines during pregnancy. Descriptively, among all infants hospitalized with ARI, 161 of 499 (32%) born to RSVpreF-unvaccinated mothers had severe LRTD, while 87 of 513 (17%) born to RSVpreF-vaccinated mothers had severe LRTD. Conclusions and Relevance Findings in this case-control study demonstrate high year-round effectiveness of RSVpreF vaccination against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants 6 months of age or younger in the first year following introduction in Australia, with the highest VE observed in the earliest age intervals. Future analyses with larger sample sizes will evaluate VE among additional subgroups.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the effectiveness of maternal vaccination with the bivalent respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein-based vaccine (RSVpreF) in preventing infant RSV hospitalization in Australia. Using a retrospective case-control design with a test-negative approach across nine hospitals, researchers analyzed data from 1,012 infants hospitalized with acute respiratory illness (ARI) aged 6 months or younger between March 2025 and February 2026. Vaccine effectiveness (VE) was calculated using logistic regression with confounder adjustment. The primary outcome, VE against RSV lower respiratory tract disease (RSV-LRTD) hospitalization, was 77.8% overall, with higher protection observed in younger infants (86.3% for those aged 2 months or younger). Comparable VE was found for severe RSV-LRTD (80.4%) and RSV-ARI (80.8%). VE remained consistent across stratifications by gestational age at vaccination and timing of vaccination relative to delivery. The study concludes that maternal RSVpreF vaccination provides high year-round protection against RSV-associated hospitalization in infants under 6 months, particularly in early infancy, supporting its continued use as a national immunization strategy.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿住院的主要原因,2025 年之前,澳大利亚尚无孕产妇 呼吸道合胞病毒 策略来预防这一弱势群体的 RSV 疾病。该研究需要量化新引入的基于母体 RSV 预灌注 F 蛋白的 疫苗 (RSVpreF) 在预防婴儿 RSV 住院方面的有效性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在澳大利亚 9 家医院进行了一项采用测试阴性设计的回顾性病例对照研究,纳入了 2025 年 3 月 1 日至 2026 年 2 月 28 日期间因 6 个月以下急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 住院的妊娠 28 周或以后出生的婴儿。
elements_zh.methods: 疫苗 有效性 (VE) 使用逻辑回归和混杂因素调整进行估计,将 VE 计算为(1 - 调整后的比值比)× 100% 与 RSV 下呼吸道疾病 (RSV-LRTD)、严重 RSV-LRTD 和 RSV-ARI 住院治疗相比。
elements_zh.main_results: 在1012名因急性呼吸道感染住院的婴儿中,呼吸道合胞病毒下呼吸道疾病住院的疫苗保护效力为77.8%(95%置信区间,66.4%-85.3%),总体情况如下:3个月或更小婴儿为80.2%(95%置信区间,71.1%-86.5%)、2个月或更小婴儿为86.3%(95%置信区间,79.0%-91.1%)、年龄大于2个月至4个月的婴儿为68.2%(95%置信区间,42.2%-82.5%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,母亲 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 在预防 6 个月以下婴儿因 RSV 相关住院方面全年均具有很高的有效性,在最早的年龄间隔中观察到的保护效果最高。这是澳大利亚继全国推广后首次对孕产妇 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 有效性进行全年评估。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持继续使用母体 RSVpreF 疫苗接种 作为减少婴儿 RSV 相关住院的主要策略,特别是在风险最高的生命前两个月。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其回顾性设计和对医院数据的依赖而受到限制,这些数据可能无法涵盖社区中的所有 RSV 病例。尽管如此,大样本量和多种结果的一致的 VE 估计强化了证据。未来计划使用更大的样本量进行分析,以评估其他亚组。

title: Kinetics and characterization of extracellular vesicle release from cells infected with a clinical isolate of respiratory syncytial virus A (ON1 genotype)
abstract: Abstract Despite the recent approval of preventive measures, the disease burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in children and older adults remains significant. To improve understanding of RSV disease, this study characterized extracellular microvesicles (EMVs) secreted during in vitro infection with a clinical RSV-A (ON1 genotype) strain (RSV/40G-A), isolated in 2022 from a pediatric pneumonia case. The type and content of EMVs released by A549 and BEAS-2B respiratory epithelial cells infected with this clinical isolate were analyzed up to 96 h post-infection (hpi). RSV infection induced a time-dependent increase in EMV levels compared to uninfected controls. EMVs released by infected BEAS-2B and A549 cells contained increasing levels of RSV nucleocapsid protein (RSV-NP) and viral RNA with a peak at 72 hpi. These findings suggest that the kinetics of vesicular release and EMV content are modulated during RSV infection. EMV secretion by host cells may constitute a potential mechanism for intercellular communication or immune activation.

title: Respiratory syncytial virus outbreaks in healthcare facilities: A review of the literature.
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory infections. Outbreaks have occurred in various healthcare settings. We reviewed RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. PubMed was searched from 2010 to 2025 for articles on RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. Eighteen articles presenting 19 RSV outbreaks were reviewed. Eleven outbreaks occurred in hematology/oncology/transplantation wards/units, six in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), and two in geriatric hospitals/long-term care facilities (LTCFs). The mean attack rate across all outbreaks was 26.04% (range: 12.00%-68.96%) and the mean duration was 39.9 (range: 5-131) days. A mean of 20.31 (range: 4-63) patients were affected per outbreak. Asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare personnel (HCP) were the most frequent sources of infection. RSV disease was particularly severe in premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients. Prolonged virus shedding also occurred among premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients, challenging the containment of outbreaks. The overall case fatality rate (CFR) among RSV-infected patients was 11.64% (mean CFR: 13.99% in hematology/oncology/transplantation units, 6.49% in NICUs, and 6.25% in geriatric clinics). Palivizumab prophylaxis was temporally associated with outbreak control when used as part of multimodal interventions. In conclusion, serious RSV outbreaks occur in healthcare facilities caring for vulnerable patients. Such outbreaks are frequently traced to HCP, usually last several weeks, and affect many patients, which emphasize the transmission dynamics of RSV within healthcare facilities but also disclose gaps in infection control. Elderly patients, residents of LTCFs, and immunocompromised patients should be vaccinated against RSV. Palivizumab prophylaxis should be studied.

title_original: Respiratory syncytial virus outbreaks in healthcare facilities: A review of the literature.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; Orthopneumovirus hominis, including RSV-A and RSV-B) outbreaks in healthcare facilities, focusing on vulnerable patient populations such as premature neonates, immunosuppressed patients, and elderly residents of long-term care facilities. The central question addresses the transmission dynamics, severity, and control of RSV outbreaks within these settings.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that searched PubMed from 2010 to 2025 for articles on RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. Eighteen articles presenting 19 outbreaks were included, covering hematology/oncology/transplantation wards (11 outbreaks), neonatal intensive care units (6 outbreaks), and geriatric hospitals/long-term care facilities (2 outbreaks).
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities are frequent, often traced to asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare personnel, and typically last several weeks. The mean attack rate across outbreaks was 26.04% (range: 12.00%-68.96%), with a mean duration of 39.9 days (range: 5-131 days). The overall case fatality rate among infected patients was 11.64%, with higher rates in hematology/oncology/transplantation units (13.99%) compared to neonatal intensive care units (6.49%) and geriatric clinics (6.25%).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Prolonged virus shedding in premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients challenges outbreak containment, and the review highlights gaps in infection control practices. The evidence base is limited to 19 outbreaks across specific high-risk settings, leaving uncertainty about transmission dynamics in other healthcare environments and populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Priority research should investigate the role of asymptomatic healthcare personnel in RSV transmission and evaluate multimodal interventions, including palivizumab prophylaxis, for outbreak control. Enhanced surveillance and infection control measures are needed in high-risk units, particularly for elderly and immunocompromised patients, to reduce outbreak severity and mortality.

analysis.summary_en: This review synthesizes evidence on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) outbreaks in healthcare facilities, focusing on vulnerable populations such as premature neonates, immunosuppressed patients, and elderly residents. Across 19 outbreaks, RSV demonstrated high attack rates (mean 26.04%) and prolonged durations (mean 39.9 days), with healthcare personnel often serving as asymptomatic sources. The overall case fatality rate was 11.64%, with the highest burden in hematology/oncology/transplantation units. Key gaps include challenges in containing outbreaks due to prolonged shedding in high-risk patients and limited evidence from diverse healthcare settings. Research priorities include investigating transmission dynamics, evaluating multimodal interventions like palivizumab, and strengthening infection control in high-risk units.

title_zh: 医疗机构中的 呼吸道合胞病毒 暴发:文献综述。
source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory infections. Outbreaks have occurred in various healthcare settings. We reviewed RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. PubMed was searched from 2010 to 2025 for articles on RSV outbreaks in healthcare facilities. Eighteen articles presenting 19 RSV outbreaks were reviewed. Eleven outbreaks occurred in hematology/oncology/transplantation wards/units, six in neonatal intensive care units (NICUs), and two in geriatric hospitals/long-term care facilities (LTCFs). The mean attack rate across all outbreaks was 26.04% (range: 12.00%-68.96%) and the mean duration was 39.9 (range: 5-131) days. A mean of 20.31 (range: 4-63) patients were affected per outbreak. Asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic healthcare personnel (HCP) were the most frequent sources of infection. RSV disease was particularly severe in premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients. Prolonged virus shedding also occurred among premature neonates and immunosuppressed patients, challenging the containment of outbreaks. The overall case fatality rate (CFR) among RSV-infected patients was 11.64% (mean CFR: 13.99% in hematology/oncology/transplantation units, 6.49% in NICUs, and 6.25% in geriatric clinics). Palivizumab prophylaxis was temporally associated with outbreak control when used as part of multimodal interventions. In conclusion, serious RSV outbreaks occur in healthcare facilities caring for vulnerable patients. Such outbreaks are frequently traced to HCP, usually last several weeks, and affect many patients, which emphasize the transmission dynamics of RSV within healthcare facilities but also disclose gaps in infection control. Elderly patients, residents of LTCFs, and immunocompromised patients should be vaccinated against RSV. Palivizumab prophylaxis should be studied.

title: Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Adults in India: An Under-recognized Public Health Concern Demanding Urgent Immunization Action.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important global cause of acute respiratory tract infection, contributing substantially to illness, hospitalization, and deaths across all age groups worldwide. While RSV has long been associated with severe disease in infants and young children, its impact on older adults is increasingly recognized, with evidence suggesting that mortality in elderly populations may equal or exceed that in paediatric age groups. In India, demographic transition, increasing prevalence of chronic comorbidities, and limited adult vaccination programmes are likely to amplify the burden of RSV disease, which remains under-recognized and insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The article delineates the burden of RSV among Indian adults, assesses current evidence and regulatory status of RSV vaccines, and identifies priorities for strengthening surveillance, informing policy, and advancing immunization efforts. CONTENT: Although national adult-specific RSV data from India remain scarce, available evidence indicates that RSV is an important contributor to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized adults, with a substantial disease burden among older adults in India. Three vaccines-GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo and Moderna mRNA-1345 are currently approved for adults ≥60 years in the United States and Europe. Early real world data from United Kingdom demonstrates significant reduction in RSV related hospitalizations following vaccine introduction within a single season [19]. In India, CDSCO conditionally approved Phase III trials of RSVPreF in June 2025, but no adult RSV vaccine is licensed for use. This review proposes for integration of routine RSV molecular testing and reporting with outcome especially in comorbid adults, inclusion of RSV vaccination in National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) deliberations for elder and high-risk groups, accelerated regulatory pathways leveraging global bridging data and implementation of prospective multicenter studies to generate robust evidence for health technology assessment, cost-effectiveness and policy formulation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a major global cause of acute respiratory tract infections with substantial morbidity and mortality across all age groups, yet its burden in older adults and in India remains under-characterized and under-recognized. The study addresses the knowledge gap regarding RSV disease burden among Indian adults and the regulatory status of adult RSV vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review that synthesizes existing evidence on RSV burden in Indian adults and evaluates the regulatory landscape of adult RSV vaccines. It focuses on hospitalized adults, particularly older adults with comorbidities, and discusses surveillance priorities and policy needs in India.
analysis.methods: The review integrates published evidence on RSV epidemiology in adults, regulatory approvals of RSV vaccines in other regions, and real-world effectiveness data from the United Kingdom. It proposes integration of routine RSV molecular testing, inclusion of RSV vaccination in national immunization deliberations, and implementation of multicenter studies to generate robust evidence.
analysis.main_results: The review highlights that RSV contributes substantially to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized Indian adults, with a notable burden among older adults. It notes that three vaccines (GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo, Moderna mRNA-1345) are approved for adults aged 60 years and older in the United States and Europe, and that India has conditionally approved Phase III trials for RSVPreF but no adult RSV vaccine is currently licensed.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that RSV in Indian adults is under-recognized and likely underestimated, particularly in high-risk groups, and emphasize the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, policy integration, and vaccine deployment. The novelty lies in synthesizing Indian-specific gaps and proposing actionable steps for surveillance and immunization.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritizing RSV molecular testing in comorbid adults, including RSV vaccination in national immunization policy deliberations, and accelerating regulatory pathways leveraging global data to inform health technology assessment and cost-effectiveness analyses in India.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base relies on a narrative review of limited national adult-specific data from India, which constrains generalizability and precision. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of robust, India-specific adult RSV burden estimates and the reliance on extrapolated data from other regions.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review examines the burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) among adults in India, highlighting its under-recognition and substantial contribution to severe acute respiratory infections, particularly in older adults with comorbidities. The authors synthesize evidence on RSV epidemiology, regulatory approvals of adult RSV vaccines in other regions, and real-world effectiveness data, noting that three vaccines are approved for adults aged 60 years and older in the United States and Europe. In India, Phase III trials for RSVPreF have been conditionally approved, but no adult RSV vaccine is currently licensed. The review emphasizes the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, integration of RSV molecular testing in high-risk groups, inclusion of RSV vaccination in national immunization policy deliberations, and accelerated regulatory pathways leveraging global data. While the findings underscore the importance of addressing RSV in Indian adults, the evidence base is limited by scarce national adult-specific data, resulting in a moderate strength of evidence.

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: RSV is a major global cause of acute respiratory tract infections with substantial morbidity and mortality across all age groups, yet its burden in older adults and in India remains under-characterized and under-recognized. The study addresses the knowledge gap regarding RSV disease burden among Indian adults and the regulatory status of adult RSV vaccines.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review that synthesizes existing evidence on RSV burden in Indian adults and evaluates the regulatory landscape of adult RSV vaccines. It focuses on hospitalized adults, particularly older adults with comorbidities, and discusses surveillance priorities and policy needs in India.
analysis_en.methods: The review integrates published evidence on RSV epidemiology in adults, regulatory approvals of RSV vaccines in other regions, and real-world effectiveness data from the United Kingdom. It proposes integration of routine RSV molecular testing, inclusion of RSV vaccination in national immunization deliberations, and implementation of multicenter studies to generate robust evidence.
analysis_en.main_results: The review highlights that RSV contributes substantially to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized Indian adults, with a notable burden among older adults. It notes that three vaccines (GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo, Moderna mRNA-1345) are approved for adults aged 60 years and older in the United States and Europe, and that India has conditionally approved Phase III trials for RSVPreF but no adult RSV vaccine is currently licensed.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence that RSV in Indian adults is under-recognized and likely underestimated, particularly in high-risk groups, and emphasize the urgent need for strengthened surveillance, policy integration, and vaccine deployment. The novelty lies in synthesizing Indian-specific gaps and proposing actionable steps for surveillance and immunization.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritizing RSV molecular testing in comorbid adults, including RSV vaccination in national immunization policy deliberations, and accelerating regulatory pathways leveraging global data to inform health technology assessment and cost-effectiveness analyses in India.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence base relies on a narrative review of limited national adult-specific data from India, which constrains generalizability and precision. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the absence of robust, India-specific adult RSV burden estimates and the reliance on extrapolated data from other regions.

title_zh: 印度成人中的 呼吸道合胞病毒:一个未被充分认识的公共卫生问题,需要采取紧急免疫行动。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important global cause of acute respiratory tract infection, contributing substantially to illness, hospitalization, and deaths across all age groups worldwide. While RSV has long been associated with severe disease in infants and young children, its impact on older adults is increasingly recognized, with evidence suggesting that mortality in elderly populations may equal or exceed that in paediatric age groups. In India, demographic transition, increasing prevalence of chronic comorbidities, and limited adult vaccination programmes are likely to amplify the burden of RSV disease, which remains under-recognized and insufficiently characterized. OBJECTIVES: The article delineates the burden of RSV among Indian adults, assesses current evidence and regulatory status of RSV vaccines, and identifies priorities for strengthening surveillance, informing policy, and advancing immunization efforts. CONTENT: Although national adult-specific RSV data from India remain scarce, available evidence indicates that RSV is an important contributor to severe acute respiratory infections in hospitalized adults, with a substantial disease burden among older adults in India. Three vaccines-GSK Arexvy, Pfizer Abrysvo and Moderna mRNA-1345 are currently approved for adults ≥60 years in the United States and Europe. Early real world data from United Kingdom demonstrates significant reduction in RSV related hospitalizations following vaccine introduction within a single season [19]. In India, CDSCO conditionally approved Phase III trials of RSVPreF in June 2025, but no adult RSV vaccine is licensed for use. This review proposes for integration of routine RSV molecular testing and reporting with outcome especially in comorbid adults, inclusion of RSV vaccination in National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) deliberations for elder and high-risk groups, accelerated regulatory pathways leveraging global bridging data and implementation of prospective multicenter studies to generate robust evidence for health technology assessment, cost-effectiveness and policy formulation.
abstract_zh: 背景:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是全球急性呼吸道感染的重要原因,在很大程度上导致全球所有年龄段的疾病、住院和死亡。虽然 RSV 长期以来一直与婴儿和幼儿的严重疾病相关,但人们越来越认识到它对老年人的影响,有证据表明老年人群中的 死亡率 可能等于或超过儿科年龄组的 死亡率。在印度,人口结构转变、慢性合并症 患病率 的增加以及成人 疫苗接种 计划的有限可能会加剧 RSV 疾病的负担,而 RSV 疾病仍然未被充分认识和充分表征。目标:本文描述了印度成年人中 RSV 的负担,评估了 RSV 疫苗 的当前证据和监管状况,并确定了加强 疫苗、为政策提供信息和推进免疫工作的优先事项。内容:尽管印度全国成人特定 RSV 数据仍然稀缺,但现有证据表明,RSV 是住院成人严重急性呼吸道感染的重要诱因,给印度老年人带来了巨大的疾病负担。疫苗-GSK Arexvy、辉瑞 Abrysvo 和 Moderna mRNA-1345 三种药物目前已在美国和欧洲获批用于 60 岁以上成人。来自英国的早期真实世界数据表明,在 疫苗 引入后,单一季节内 RSV 相关住院率显着减少 [19]。在印度,CDSCO 于 2025 年 6 月有条件批准了 RSVPreF 的 III 期试验,但没有成人 RSV 疫苗 获得使用许可。本次审查建议将常规 RSV 分子检测和报告与结果相结合,特别是在合并症成人中,将 RSV 疫苗接种 纳入国家免疫技术咨询组 (NTAGI) 对老年人和高危人群的审议,加速利用全球桥接数据的监管途径,并实施前瞻性多中心研究,为卫生技术评估、成本效益和政策制定提供强有力的证据。

title: Live human metapneumovirus vaccine candidates attenuated by temperature sensitivity mutations from human respiratory syncytial virus
abstract: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV, genus Metapneumovirus ) and respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV, genus Orthopneumovirus ) are pediatric respiratory pathogens of the Pneumoviridae family. We previously developed live-intranasal HRSV vaccine candidates attenuated by genetically stabilized temperature sensitivity/attenuating ( ts/att ) mutations in the HRSV polymerase (L) ORF, including sites “ 1030s ” (L codon changes S1313 (AGC-to-TCA) /Y1321K (AAA) , named after clone number 1030), and “Δ1313/I1314L,” comprising a genetically stabilized deletion of L codon 1313. In pediatric vaccine studies, HRSV candidates with “ 1030s ” or Δ1313/I1314L were attenuated, immunogenic, and genetically stable. Given the similarities between HRSV and HMPV, we introduced corresponding modifications into the HMPV L ORF, resulting in HMPV with deletion of codon 1238 (Δ1238), corresponding to HRSV Δ1313/I1314L, and HMPV with C1238S (TCA) /Y1246K (AAA) substitutions together (C1238S/Y1246K, corresponding to HRSV “ 1030s ”), or individually (C1238S, Y1246K), serving as experimental controls. All versions replicated well in Vero cells at 32°C. At 37°C, replication of Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, and Y1246K was delayed, and peak titers were ~80-fold, 200-fold, and 25-fold lower than wild-type HMPV. As predicted, the C1238S control was not temperature-sensitive (shutoff temperature [ T SH ] > 40°C, similar to wild-type HMPV), while Y1246K and Δ1238 ( T SH = 39°C) and C1238S/Y1246K ( T SH = 38°C) had a ts phenotype. Thus, the addition of the C1238S (TCA) substitution increased the temperature sensitivity of Y1246K. The HMPV ts/att sites were genetically stable under temperature stress. In hamsters inoculated intranasally, C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 were restricted in replication, yet immunogenic and protective against HMPV challenge. Thus, inclusion in the HMPV L ORF of C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 mutations, corresponding to HRSV ts/att sites, provided genetically stable live-attenuated HMPV, suitable for clinical development. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory illness in young children, and there are no licensed vaccines. Similarly to immunization strategies against the related human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV), live-attenuated HMPV vaccines for intranasal immunization would be most suitable for young children. Live-intranasal vaccines infect and induce immunity in the presence of residual maternal antibodies without priming for enhanced respiratory disease. Genetic stability of attenuating mutations represents a challenge in vaccine design. We generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing into corresponding sites of the HMPV polymerase gene temperature-sensitivity-inducing attenuating mutations that had been originally developed for HRSV, genetically stabilized, and proven to be free of reversions in HRSV vaccine studies. The resulting HMPV vaccine candidates are temperature-sensitive, attenuated, and genetically stable under temperature stress. In the hamster model, the new HMPV candidates were immunogenic and protective. These live-attenuated HMPV candidates will be advanced to pediatric vaccine studies.

title_original: Live human metapneumovirus vaccine candidates attenuated by temperature sensitivity mutations from human respiratory syncytial virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory illness in young children, and there are no licensed vaccines. Given the similarities between HMPV and the related human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV), the study aimed to develop live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations originally developed for HRSV into the HMPV polymerase gene.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations into the HMPV polymerase (L) ORF, including Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, C1238S, and Y1246K. Replication and genetic stability were assessed in Vero cells at 32°C and 37°C, and the immunogenicity and protective efficacy were evaluated in hamsters inoculated intranasally.
analysis.methods: HMPV vaccine candidates were engineered by introducing HRSV-derived temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations into the HMPV L ORF, including Δ1238 (corresponding to HRSV Δ1313/I1314L) and C1238S/Y1246K (corresponding to HRSV “1030s”). Replication kinetics were measured in Vero cells at 32°C and 37°C, and temperature sensitivity was determined by shutoff temperature (T_SH). Genetic stability was assessed under temperature stress, and immunogenicity and protection were evaluated in hamsters after intranasal inoculation.
analysis.main_results: At 37°C, replication of Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, and Y1246K was delayed, with peak titers approximately 80-fold, 200-fold, and 25-fold lower than wild-type HMPV, respectively. The C1238S control was not temperature-sensitive (T_SH > 40°C), while Y1246K and Δ1238 (T_SH = 39°C) and C1238S/Y1246K (T_SH = 38°C) exhibited a temperature-sensitive phenotype. The C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 candidates were restricted in replication in hamsters but were immunogenic and protective against HMPV challenge.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The introduction of HRSV-derived temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations into the HMPV L ORF generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates that are temperature-sensitive, attenuated, genetically stable, immunogenic, and protective in a hamster model. This approach leverages previously validated HRSV mutations, demonstrating a novel strategy for HMPV vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the advancement of live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates to pediatric clinical studies, offering a potential solution to the unmet need for HMPV vaccination in young children. The genetically stable temperature-sensitive mutations provide a robust platform for further development and evaluation.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro and in a hamster model, which may not fully recapitulate human infection or immune responses. While the temperature-sensitive mutations were genetically stable under temperature stress, their stability and safety in humans remain to be confirmed. The evidence strength is moderate due to the preclinical nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed live-attenuated human metapneumovirus (HMPV) vaccine candidates by introducing temperature-sensitivity/attenuating mutations originally derived from human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) into the HMPV polymerase gene. elements_zh.main_results: 在37°C下,Δ1238、C1238S/Y1246K和Y1246K的复制被延迟,峰值滴度分别比野生型HMPV低约80倍、200倍和25倍。C1238S对照对温度不敏感(T_SH > 40°C),而Y1246K和Δ1238(T_SH = 39°C)和C1238S/Y1246K(T_SH = 38°C)表现出温度敏感表型。C1238S/Y1246K 和 Δ1238 候选物在仓鼠中的复制受到限制,但具有免疫原性并能抵抗 HMPV 攻击。

elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持将减毒活 HMPV 疫苗 候选药物推进儿科临床研究,为幼儿对 HMPV 疫苗接种 未满足的需求提供潜在的解决方案。基因稳定的温度敏感 突变 为进一步开发和评估提供了强大的平台。

title_zh: 活人类偏肺病毒 疫苗 候选物因来自人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 的温度敏感性 突变 减毒
source_body_en: ABSTRACT Human metapneumovirus (HMPV, genus Metapneumovirus ) and respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV, genus Orthopneumovirus ) are pediatric respiratory pathogens of the Pneumoviridae family. We previously developed live-intranasal HRSV vaccine candidates attenuated by genetically stabilized temperature sensitivity/attenuating ( ts/att ) mutations in the HRSV polymerase (L) ORF, including sites “ 1030s ” (L codon changes S1313 (AGC-to-TCA) /Y1321K (AAA) , named after clone number 1030), and “Δ1313/I1314L,” comprising a genetically stabilized deletion of L codon 1313. In pediatric vaccine studies, HRSV candidates with “ 1030s ” or Δ1313/I1314L were attenuated, immunogenic, and genetically stable. Given the similarities between HRSV and HMPV, we introduced corresponding modifications into the HMPV L ORF, resulting in HMPV with deletion of codon 1238 (Δ1238), corresponding to HRSV Δ1313/I1314L, and HMPV with C1238S (TCA) /Y1246K (AAA) substitutions together (C1238S/Y1246K, corresponding to HRSV “ 1030s ”), or individually (C1238S, Y1246K), serving as experimental controls. All versions replicated well in Vero cells at 32°C. At 37°C, replication of Δ1238, C1238S/Y1246K, and Y1246K was delayed, and peak titers were ~80-fold, 200-fold, and 25-fold lower than wild-type HMPV. As predicted, the C1238S control was not temperature-sensitive (shutoff temperature [ T SH ] > 40°C, similar to wild-type HMPV), while Y1246K and Δ1238 ( T SH = 39°C) and C1238S/Y1246K ( T SH = 38°C) had a ts phenotype. Thus, the addition of the C1238S (TCA) substitution increased the temperature sensitivity of Y1246K. The HMPV ts/att sites were genetically stable under temperature stress. In hamsters inoculated intranasally, C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 were restricted in replication, yet immunogenic and protective against HMPV challenge. Thus, inclusion in the HMPV L ORF of C1238S/Y1246K and Δ1238 mutations, corresponding to HRSV ts/att sites, provided genetically stable live-attenuated HMPV, suitable for clinical development. IMPORTANCE Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory illness in young children, and there are no licensed vaccines. Similarly to immunization strategies against the related human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV), live-attenuated HMPV vaccines for intranasal immunization would be most suitable for young children. Live-intranasal vaccines infect and induce immunity in the presence of residual maternal antibodies without priming for enhanced respiratory disease. Genetic stability of attenuating mutations represents a challenge in vaccine design. We generated live-attenuated HMPV vaccine candidates by introducing into corresponding sites of the HMPV polymerase gene temperature-sensitivity-inducing attenuating mutations that had been originally developed for HRSV, genetically stabilized, and proven to be free of reversions in HRSV vaccine studies. The resulting HMPV vaccine candidates are temperature-sensitive, attenuated, and genetically stable under temperature stress. In the hamster model, the new HMPV candidates were immunogenic and protective. These live-attenuated HMPV candidates will be advanced to pediatric vaccine studies.

title: Household Transmission Dynamics of Human Respiratory Syncytial Virus in China: A Multicentre Epidemiological and Molecular Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To estimate the secondary HRSV infection proportion, age-specific susceptibility, inferred spread, and HRSV-A/B transmission patterns in Chinese households. METHODS: This prospective case-ascertained household cohort in Zhejiang, China (November 2024-December 2025) recruited medically attended, laboratory-confirmed paediatric HRSV index cases aged 0-14 years. Ten-day exposure histories, Day 3/10 contact sampling, and regression models assessed household- and contact-level risk factors. The study focused on estimating secondary infection rates, age-specific susceptibility, and transmission patterns between HRSV-A and HRSV-B. It recruited 179 households with 542 contacts, including 110 households with secondary infections and 218 contacts infected. title: Large increase in mortality and hospital admissions among young children and the aged due to Influenza and Respiratory Syncytial Virus in Brazil in 2025
abstract: Background: Mortality and hospital admissions due to Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) peaked between January and August 2025 in Brazil. Methods: The Brazilian Ministry of Health data on hospital admissions and deaths caused by SARI were compiled by age group (<5, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and quarter between January 2023 and June 2025. SARI causes were aggregated into SARS-Cov-2, Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and other viruses (parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, metapneumovirus). Multinomial regression was used to impute likely causes of death when these were not laboratory confirmed. Results: In the second quarter of 2025 (2025/2), RSV mortality rate among children <5 years reached 60 per 100,000, which is a 43% increase compared with 2024/2. Mortality rate for the joint impact of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus in the same age group doubled from 20 to 40 on the same scale in 2025/2 compared to 2024/2. Over the same period, influenza mortality tripled among the aged, whereas mortality due to other respiratory viruses increased less dramatically, except for SARS-CoV-2, which decreased among the aged from 150 to 25 per 100,000 between 2023/1 and 2025/2. Other age groups remained relatively stable over the period. The variation in hospital admissions largely followed that of mortality. Conclusions: While deaths and hospital admissions caused by SARS-CoV-2 declined rapidly since 2023, mortality rates of other respiratory viruses, mainly influenza and RSV, increased significantly among children <5 years and the aged in 2025/2. Public health policies that facilitate vaccine uptake against these infections should be given high priority.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unexplained surge in severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) mortality and hospital admissions in Brazil during 2025, particularly among young children and older adults, where the role of specific respiratory viruses remained unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study compiled Brazilian Ministry of Health data on SARI hospital admissions and deaths by age group (<5, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and quarter from January 2023 to June 2025.
analysis.methods: SARI causes were aggregated into SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and other viruses (parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, metapneumovirus). Multinomial regression was used to impute likely causes of death when laboratory confirmation was absent.
analysis.main_results: In the second quarter of 2025, RSV mortality among children under 5 years reached 60 per 100,000, a 43% increase compared with the same period in 2024. Mortality for the combined group of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus doubled from 20 to 40 per 100,000 in the same age group. Influenza mortality tripled among the aged, while SARS-CoV-2 mortality decreased from 150 to 25 per 100,000 in this group between 2023/1 and 2025/2.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that while SARS-CoV-2-related mortality declined, mortality due to influenza and RSV increased significantly among children under 5 years and older adults in 2025/2, highlighting a shift in the burden of respiratory viruses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for public health policies prioritizing vaccine uptake against influenza and RSV, particularly in high-risk groups such as young children and older adults.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on aggregated national surveillance data with imputation for unconfirmed causes, which may introduce misclassification bias and limit causal inference; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these methodological constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed Brazilian Ministry of Health data on severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) hospital admissions and deaths from January 2023 to June 2025, stratified by age group and quarter. Using aggregated causes of SARI and multinomial regression for imputation of unconfirmed deaths, the authors observed a marked increase in mortality due to Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) among children under 5 years in the second quarter of 2025, with a 43% rise compared to 2024. Influenza mortality tripled among older adults during the same period, while SARS-CoV-2 mortality declined substantially. The variation in hospital admissions mirrored mortality trends. The authors interpret these findings as a shift in the burden of respiratory viruses, emphasizing the urgent need for enhanced vaccine strategies targeting influenza and RSV in high-risk populations.

elements_zh.methods: SARI 病因汇总为 SARS-CoV-2、流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和其他病毒(副流感病毒、腺病毒、鼻病毒、博卡病毒、偏肺病毒)。当缺乏实验室确认时,使用多项回归来估算可能的死亡原因。
elements_zh.main_results: In the second quarter of 2025, RSV mortality among children under 5 years reached 60 per 100,000, a 43% increase compared with the same period in 2024. Mortality for the combined group of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus doubled from 20 to 40 per 100,000 in the same age group. Influenza mortality tripled among the aged, while SARS-CoV-2 mortality decreased from 150 to 25 per 100,000 in this group between 2023/1 and 2025/2.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出的结论是,虽然 SARS-CoV-2 相关的 死亡率 有所下降,但 2025/2 年 5 岁以下儿童和老年人中流感和 RSV 导致的 死亡率 显着增加,凸显了呼吸道病毒负担的变化。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调,公共卫生政策需要优先考虑 疫苗 对抗流感和 RSV 的作用,特别是在幼儿和老年人等高危人群中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究依赖于汇总的国家 监测 数据,并对未经证实的原因进行插补,这可能会引入错误分类偏差并限制因果推断;由于这些方法学限制,证据强度被评估为中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the unexplained surge in severe acute respiratory infection (SARI) mortality and hospital admissions in Brazil during 2025, particularly among young children and older adults, where the role of specific respiratory viruses remained unclear.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study compiled Brazilian Ministry of Health data on SARI hospital admissions and deaths by age group (<5, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and quarter from January 2023 to June 2025.
analysis_en.methods: SARI causes were aggregated into SARS-CoV-2, Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and other viruses (parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, metapneumovirus). Multinomial regression was used to impute likely causes of death when laboratory confirmation was absent.
analysis_en.main_results: In the second quarter of 2025, RSV mortality among children under 5 years reached 60 per 100,000, a 43% increase compared with the same period in 2024. Mortality for the combined group of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus doubled from 20 to 40 per 100,000 in the same age group. Influenza mortality tripled among the aged, while SARS-CoV-2 mortality decreased from 150 to 25 per 100,000 in this group between 2023/1 and 2025/2.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that while SARS-CoV-2-related mortality declined, mortality due to influenza and RSV increased significantly among children under 5 years and older adults in 2025/2, highlighting a shift in the burden of respiratory viruses.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the need for public health policies prioritizing vaccine uptake against influenza and RSV, particularly in high-risk groups such as young children and older adults.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on aggregated national surveillance data with imputation for unconfirmed causes, which may introduce misclassification bias and limit causal inference; the evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these methodological constraints.

title_zh: 2025 年巴西流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 导致幼儿和老年人的 死亡率 和住院人数大幅增加
source_body_en: Background: Mortality and hospital admissions due to Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) peaked between January and August 2025 in Brazil. Methods: The Brazilian Ministry of Health data on hospital admissions and deaths caused by SARI were compiled by age group (<5, 5-14, 15-49, 50-64, 65+ years) and quarter between January 2023 and June 2025. SARI causes were aggregated into SARS-Cov-2, Influenza, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and other viruses (parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, metapneumovirus). Multinomial regression was used to impute likely causes of death when these were not laboratory confirmed. Results: In the second quarter of 2025 (2025/2), RSV mortality rate among children <5 years reached 60 per 100,000, which is a 43% increase compared with 2024/2. Mortality rate for the joint impact of parainfluenza, adenovirus, rhinovirus, bocavirus, and metapneumovirus in the same age group doubled from 20 to 40 on the same scale in 2025/2 compared to 2024/2. Over the same period, influenza mortality tripled among the aged, whereas mortality due to other respiratory viruses increased less dramatically, except for SARS-CoV-2, which decreased among the aged from 150 to 25 per 100,000 between 2023/1 and 2025/2. Other age groups remained relatively stable over the period. The variation in hospital admissions largely followed that of mortality. Conclusions: While deaths and hospital admissions caused by SARS-CoV-2 declined rapidly since 2023, mortality rates of other respiratory viruses, mainly influenza and RSV, increased significantly among children <5 years and the aged in 2025/2. Public health policies that facilitate vaccine uptake against these infections should be given high priority.

title: Kiến thức, thái độ và dự định tiêm vắc xin phòng vi rút hợp bào hô hấp của khách hàng tại Phòng tiêm chủng Trường Đại học Y Hà Nội năm 2025 Knowledge, attitude and intention to receive the respiratory syncytial virus vaccine among clients attending the Immunization Clinic of Hanoi Medical University in 2025
abstract: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện trên 425 đối tượng từ 18 tuổi trở lên tại phòng tiêm chủng trườngĐại học Y Hà Nội năm 2025, được tiến hành từ tháng 11/2025 đến tháng 5/2026. Mục tiêu nghiên cứunhằm đánh giá kiến thức, thái độ, dự định tiêm vắc xin phòng vi rút hợp bào hô hấp (RSV) và một số yếutố liên quan. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy phần lớn đối tượng nghiên cứu có kiến thức hạn chế về vắc xinphòng RSV (17,9%), trong đó khoảng một phần ba (35,8%) chưa từng nghe về vắc xin này. Tuy nhiên, đasố người tham gia có thái độ tích cực về vắc xin phòng RSV (63,3%). Đáng chú ý, có tới 79,1% đối tượngbày tỏ có dự định tiêm vắc xin phòng RSV với lý do chính là lo ngại về nguy cơ mắc RSV. Kết quả phântích hồi quy logistic đa biến cho thấy những người có kiến thức đạt về vắc xin có liên quan đến dự địnhtiêm cao hơn (OR = 11,35; 95%CI: 1,92 – 67,29). Tương tự, thái độ tích cực về vắc xin cũng liên quan đếndự định tiêm cao hơn (OR = 5,64; 95%CI: 2,71 – 11,74) so với nhóm có thái độ không tích cực. Ngược lại,việc tiếp cận thông tin từ bạn bè có liên quan đến dự định tiêm thấp hơn (OR = 0,29; 95% CI: 0,10 – 0,89)so với nhóm còn lại. Các yếu tố như kiến thức và thái độ tích cực đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc thúcđẩy ý định tiêm, trong khi các nguồn thông tin không chính thống có thể làm giảm niềm tin vào vắc xin. Dođó, cần tăng cường truyền thông chính thống và tư vấn y tế nhằm nâng cao nhận thức và chuyển hóa ýđịnh thành hành vi tiêm chủng thực tế.

source_records.abstract: Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện trên 425 đối tượng từ 18 tuổi trở lên tại phòng tiêm chủng trườngĐại học Y Hà Nội năm 2025, được tiến hành từ tháng 11/2025 đến tháng 5/2026. Mục tiêu nghiên cứunhằm đánh giá kiến thức, thái độ, dự định tiêm vắc xin phòng vi rút hợp bào hô hấp (RSV) và một số yếutố liên quan. Kết quả nghiên cứu cho thấy phần lớn đối tượng nghiên cứu có kiến thức hạn chế về vắc xinphòng RSV (17,9%), trong đó khoảng một phần ba (35,8%) chưa từng nghe về vắc xin này. Tuy nhiên, đasố người tham gia có thái độ tích cực về vắc xin phòng RSV (63,3%). Đáng chú ý, có tới 79,1% đối tượngbày tỏ có dự định tiêm vắc xin phòng RSV với lý do chính là lo ngại về nguy cơ mắc RSV. Kết quả phântích hồi quy logistic đa biến cho thấy những người có kiến thức đạt về vắc xin có liên quan đến dự địnhtiêm cao hơn (OR = 11,35; 95%CI: 1,92 – 67,29). Tương tự, thái độ tích cực về vắc xin cũng liên quan đếndự định tiêm cao hơn (OR = 5,64; 95%CI: 2,71 – 11,74) so với nhóm có thái độ không tích cực. Ngược lại,việc tiếp cận thông tin từ bạn bè có liên quan đến dự định tiêm thấp hơn (OR = 0,29; 95% CI: 0,10 – 0,89)so với nhóm còn lại. Các yếu tố như kiến thức và thái độ tích cực đóng vai trò quan trọng trong việc thúcđẩy ý định tiêm, trong khi các nguồn thông tin không chính thống có thể làm giảm niềm tin vào vắc xin. Dođó, cần tăng cường truyền thông chính thống và tư vấn y tế nhằm nâng cao nhận thức và chuyển hóa ýđịnh thành hành vi tiêm chủng thực tế.

title_original: Kiến thức, thái độ và dự định tiêm vắc xin phòng vi rút hợp bào hô hấp của khách hàng tại Phòng tiêm chủng Trường Đại học Y Hà Nội năm 2025 Knowledge, attitude and intention to receive the respiratory syncytial virus vaccine among clients attending the Immunization Clinic of Hanoi Medical University in 2025

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the limited public knowledge and awareness of the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine among adults in Vietnam, aiming to evaluate knowledge, attitudes, and intention to receive the vaccine. It sought to identify factors influencing vaccine acceptance in a clinical setting.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 425 adults aged 18 years or older attending the Immunization Clinic of Hanoi Medical University between November 2025 and May 2026. Participants were clients receiving vaccination services at the specified clinic during the study period.
analysis.methods: The study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and intention to receive the RSV vaccine using structured questionnaires. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with the intention to receive the vaccine, including knowledge and attitude scores.
analysis.main_results: Only 17.9% of participants had adequate knowledge about the RSV vaccine, with 35.8% having never heard of it. A majority (63.3%) held positive attitudes toward the vaccine, and 79.1% expressed intention to receive it, primarily due to concerns about RSV infection risk. Multivariable logistic regression showed that adequate knowledge (OR = 11.35; 95% CI: 1.92–67.29) and positive attitudes (OR = 5.64; 95% CI: 2.71–11.74) were strongly associated with higher intention to vaccinate, while information from friends was associated with lower intention (OR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.10–0.89).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that higher knowledge and positive attitudes significantly increased the likelihood of intending to receive the RSV vaccine, while informal information sources reduced acceptance. They highlighted the need for targeted health communication to improve vaccine uptake.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that improving public knowledge and attitudes through official health communication channels could enhance RSV vaccine acceptance and inform vaccination strategies in similar clinical settings.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by its single-center, cross-sectional design, which restricts generalizability and causal inference. The reliance on self-reported intention rather than actual vaccination behavior further constrains the strength of evidence, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study evaluated knowledge, attitudes, and intention to receive the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine among 425 adults attending an immunization clinic in Hanoi, Vietnam, from November 2025 to May 2026. It found that only 17.9% had adequate knowledge about the vaccine, with 35.8% unaware of its existence, yet 63.3% held positive attitudes and 79.1% intended to receive it, primarily due to infection risk concerns. Multivariable analysis revealed that adequate knowledge (OR = 11.35; 95% CI: 1.92–67.29) and positive attitudes (OR = 5.64; 95% CI: 2.71–11.74) strongly predicted higher vaccination intention, while information from friends reduced intention (OR = 0.29; 95% CI: 0.10–0.89). The authors concluded that targeted health communication and counseling could improve vaccine acceptance. However, the single-center design and reliance on intention rather than actual vaccination limit generalizability and causal inference.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究针对越南成年人对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗 的有限公众知识和认识的问题,旨在评估接受 疫苗 的知识、态度和意图。它试图找出影响临床环境中 疫苗 接受度的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2025年11月至2026年5月期间在河内医科大学免疫诊所就诊的425名18岁或以上成年人进行了一项横断面研究。参与者是研究期间在指定诊所接受疫苗接种服务的客户。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用结构化问卷评估了接收 RSV 疫苗 的知识、态度和意图。进行逻辑回归分析以确定与接受 疫苗 的意图相关的因素,包括知识和态度得分。
elements_zh.main_results: 只有 17.9% 的参与者对 RSV 疫苗 有足够的了解,35.8% 的参与者从未听说过。大多数人(63.3%)对疫苗持积极态度,79.1%表示有意接受,主要是出于对RSV感染风险的担忧。多变量逻辑回归显示,足够的知识(OR = 11.35;95% CI:1.92-67.29)和积极态度(OR = 5.64;95% CI:2.71-11.74)与较高的疫苗接种意愿密切相关,而来自朋友的信息与较低的接种意愿相关(OR = 0.29;95% CI:0.10-0.89)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,更高的知识和积极的态度显着增加了打算接收 RSV 疫苗 的可能性,而非正式信息来源则降低了接受度。他们强调需要进行有针对性的健康沟通,以提高 疫苗 的吸收率。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,通过官方健康沟通渠道提高公众知识和态度可以提高 RSV 疫苗 的接受度,并为类似临床环境中的 疫苗接种 策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到单中心、横截面设计的限制,限制了普遍性和因果推理。对自我报告意图而不是实际 疫苗接种 行为的依赖进一步限制了证据的强度,需要谨慎解释。

title: The outpatient economic burden of respiratory syncytial virus infection in adults aged ≥ 60 years in Germany: results from the BUCOSS study
abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infection (ARI) in adults aged ≥ 60 years, but data on its outpatient epidemiology and societal costs remain limited. Methods BUCOSS was a prospective observational study conducted over 3 seasons (2022/23–2024/25) in adults aged ≥ 60 years presenting with ARI to 29 outpatient practices in Germany. Multiplex PCR testing was performed at baseline. RSV-positive patients were prospectively followed for up to 28 days. Clinical and socioeconomic burden, including direct medical, indirect, and patient-borne out-of-pocket costs, was assessed using structured questionnaires on days 0, 14, and 28. Approximate national burden was estimated using incidence-based and ARE–prevalence-based extrapolation, including an additional scenario analysis excluding indirect costs. analysis.research_question_and_background: RSV is a leading cause of acute respiratory infection in adults aged 60 years or older, yet outpatient epidemiology and societal cost data remain sparse, creating a knowledge gap that this study aimed to address.
analysis.study_design_and_population: BUCOSS was a prospective observational study conducted across three consecutive seasons (2022/23–2024/25) in 29 outpatient practices in Germany, enrolling adults aged 60 years or older who presented with acute respiratory infection.
analysis.methods: Multiplex PCR testing was performed at baseline to confirm RSV infection, and RSV-positive patients were followed prospectively for up to 28 days using structured questionnaires administered on days 0, 14, and 28 to capture clinical and socioeconomic burden.
analysis.main_results: Among 3,261 patients with acute respiratory infection, 192 (5.9%) had PCR-confirmed RSV infection; after excluding 4 hospitalized patients, 188 were included in the outpatient cost analysis, with a mean societal cost per episode of €510.0 (SD €742.58), comprising direct medical costs of €161.3, indirect costs of €331.8, and out-of-pocket costs of €16.9.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as demonstrating that RSV imposes a substantial outpatient economic burden in older adults, with indirect costs driven predominantly by productivity losses and a notable proportion of cases occurring in patients without high-risk status.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results support the prioritization of RSV prevention strategies in aging populations and highlight the economic burden of outpatient RSV beyond inpatient care, informing public health policy and vaccine deployment decisions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s limitations include its observational design, reliance on self-reported productivity losses for indirect cost estimation, and potential underestimation of total burden due to exclusion of hospitalized cases, warranting cautious interpretation of the extrapolated national estimates.

analysis.summary_en: This prospective observational study (BUCOSS) assessed the outpatient economic burden of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in adults aged 60 years or older in Germany across three seasons (2022/23–2024/25). Among 3,261 patients with acute respiratory infection, 5.9% had PCR-confirmed RSV, with a mean societal cost per episode of €510.0, primarily driven by indirect productivity losses. Extrapolated national estimates suggest 258,000–374,000 medically attended outpatient RSV cases per season, costing €131.7–190.9 million in societal expenses. The findings underscore RSV as an economically important cause of outpatient illness in older adults and support prevention strategies in aging populations.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: BUCOSS 是一项在德国 29 个门诊诊所连续三个季度(2022/23-2024/25)进行的前瞻性观察性研究,招募了 60 岁或以上患有急性呼吸道感染的成年人。

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为,RSV 给老年人带来了沉重的门诊经济负担,间接成本主要由生产力损失造成,而且很大一部分病例发生在没有高危状态的患者中。

title: An evaluation of the anti-human respiratory syncytial virus activity of sophora alkaloids and the enhanced efficacy by liposomes via intratracheal administration
abstract: Human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections and related deaths in infants, young children, and the elderly. The clinical management of RSV is challenging due to its high mutation rate and the limited efficacy and safety of existing antiviral drugs. Sophora alkaloids, natural compounds derived from Sophora flavescens, exhibit broad-spectrum antiviral and immunomodulatory activities. Mechanistically, RSV relies on ERK1/2 phosphorylation to facilitate viral replication and spread, while sophora alkaloids inhibit ERK1/2 phosphorylation via regulating MEK/ERK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing viral proliferation and the inflammatory response caused by RSV infection. In vivo studies demonstrated that sophora alkaloids significantly reduced the mortality of RSV-infected mice via intratracheal administration. To further enhance the pulmonary retention of drugs, liposomes were used to improve the therapeutic effects of sophora alkaloids. As the most effective sophora alkaloids against RSV infection, sophocarpine (SC) was encapsulated in liposomes to enhance its anti-RSV infection effect. In vivo studies demonstrate that SC-loaded liposomes outperformed the free SC in suppressing RSV replication and alleviating pulmonary inflammation in murine models of RSV infection. This study not only clarifies the mechanism by which sophora alkaloids counteract RSV-infection but also provides liposomal formulation of SC to improve the anti-RSV therapeutic effects.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿、幼儿和老年人严重下呼吸道感染和相关死亡的主要原因。由于 RSV 的高 突变 发生率以及现有 抗病毒药物 药物的疗效和安全性有限,RSV 的临床管理具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 RSV 感染的小鼠模型进行体内研究,以评估槐树生物碱及其脂质体制剂的抗 RSV 活性。
elements_zh.methods: 槐生物碱,特别是槐果碱 (SC),被封装在脂质体中以增强肺滞留和治疗效果。作用机制涉及通过调节 MEK/ERK 信号通路抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化。
elements_zh.main_results: 体内研究表明,槐花生物碱通过气管内给药可显着降低 RSV 感染小鼠的 死亡率。在小鼠模型中,负载 SC 的脂质体在抑制 RSV 复制和减轻肺部炎症方面优于游离 SC。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究阐明,槐花生物碱通过抑制 ERK1/2 磷酸化、抑制病毒增殖和炎症反应来抵抗 RSV 感染。SC的脂质体制剂为提高抗RSV治疗效果提供了一种新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,脂质体槐果碱可能是 RSV 感染的一种有前途的治疗策略,有可能改善婴儿、幼儿和老年人等高危人群的 治疗 结局。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该证据基于体内小鼠模型,可能无法完全转化为人类临床结果。证据的强度是中等的,因为该研究在动物模型中证明了有效性,但需要在人体试验中进一步验证。

title: Evaluation of Universal Biomolecular Medium for Molecular Detection of Respiratory Viruses: A Paired, Multi-Platform Comparison
abstract: Pre-analytical variables, including specimen transport media, may influence the performance of molecular assays used for respiratory pathogen detection. Universal Biomolecular Medium (UBMTM) has been developed to support nucleic acid preservation and molecular testing, but evidence regarding its analytical compatibility with routinely used molecular platforms remains limited. We conducted a retrospective paired comparison of UBMTM against conventional transport and lysis media across multiple molecular platforms to evaluate the post-collection analytical compatibility of UBM. Residual respiratory specimens positive for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus, influenza B virus, respiratory syncytial virus, human rhinovirus, human metapneumovirus, Haemophilus influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and Bordetella pertussis were analyzed. Paired aliquots generated from the same specimen were tested using the AllplexTM SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV Assay, Xpert® Xpress CoV-2/Flu/RSV plus, Panther Fusion® SARS-CoV-2/Flu A/B/RSV Assay, and selected AllplexTM respiratory panels. Analytical agreement and cycle threshold (Ct) values were compared using paired statistical analyses and Bland–Altman methods. UBM demonstrated complete qualitative concordance with comparator media across all evaluated targets and platforms, yielding 100% positive, negative and overall agreement. Although statistically significant Ct differences were observed for selected target–platform combinations, these shifts were generally small and did not affect qualitative result interpretation. Internal control performance remained stable across media. These findings support the post-collection analytical compatibility of UBMTM with the evaluated molecular workflows.

title: Consensus based expert recommendations for management and prevention of RSV infections in older adults in emerging market countries: results from an expert panel structured survey
abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) can cause serious disease in older adults (OAs), particularly those with comorbidities. It is a leading cause of acute respiratory illness and lower respiratory tract infections in adults ≥60 years. Its impact on morbidity, mortality, and healthcare systems is becoming evident. Questions about the burden of disease (BoD) are raised due to underdiagnosis and the similarity with other respiratory illnesses. First opportunities for prevention came in 2023 and 2024, with vaccines approved for ≥60 years, expanding eligibility to additional age groups. RESEARCH DESIGN AND METHODS: A modified Delphi approach through a questionnaire survey and virtual consensus workshop with 27 experts in respiratory and infectious diseases from 12 emerging market countries was done to reach consensus on diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of RSV in OAs. RESULTS: The panel recommends the introduction of a universal vaccination program for all adults aged ≥70 years, and vaccination for all adults aged ≥60 years with comorbidities. The need for increased awareness, better testing, and national and international guidelines was also agreed. CONCLUSION: The agreements highlight that RSV vaccination for OAs should be prioritized. Educating clinicians and patients, improving surveillance, and integrating RSV vaccination into health policies are key to reducing BoD in OAs.

abstract_zh: 背景:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 可导致老年人 (OA) 患严重疾病,尤其是患有合并症的老年人。它是 60 岁以上成人急性呼吸道疾病和下呼吸道感染的主要原因。它对发病率、死亡率 和医疗保健系统的影响正变得越来越明显。由于诊断不足以及与其他呼吸道疾病的相似性,人们对疾病负担 (BoD) 提出了疑问。第一次预防机会出现在 2023 年和 2024 年,疫苗 获得批准的年龄≥60 岁,将资格扩大到其他年龄组。研究设计和方法:采用改良的德尔菲法,通过问卷调查和来自 12 个新兴市场国家的 27 名呼吸道和传染病专家参加的虚拟共识研讨会,就 OA 中 RSV 的 诊断、预防和 治疗 达成共识。结果:专家组建议为所有年龄≥70岁的成年人引入通用的疫苗接种计划,并为所有年龄≥60岁有合并症的成年人引入疫苗接种。还同意需要提高认识、更好的测试以及国家和国际指南。结论:协议强调应优先考虑用于 OA 的 RSV 疫苗接种。对临床医生和患者进行教育、改进 监测 并将 RSV 疫苗接种 纳入卫生政策是减少 OA 中 BoD 的关键。

title: Pediatricians’ attitudes and knowledge of RSV immunization products: A multi-country cross-sectional survey
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Nirsevimab and the maternal vaccination in pregnancy are newly introduced prevention strategies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). This study evaluated pediatricians' knowledge, attitudes, and barriers to RSV immunization in Italy and Cyprus/Greece, where nirsevimab had not yet been implemented, and in Spain, where it was introduced in 2023/2024. METHODS: A survey was distributed to pediatricians across Spain, Italy, and Cyprus/Greece in July-August/2024. Occupational characteristics, and knowledge, attitudes and practices toward palivizumab, nirsevimab, and the maternal vaccine were collected. Of 578 respondents (response rate = 19.3%), 50% were from Spain, 40% from Italy, and 10% from Cyprus/Greece. As 90% of responses came from Spain and Italy, the main analysis focused on these two countries. Descriptive and univariate analyses (Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests) were conducted. RESULTS: Respondents included pediatricians from community (51.7%), tertiary (30.4%), and primary/secondary care (17.9%) settings. Pediatricians were generally aware of RSV risk factors, without differences across countries. However, 245 (55.9%) and 375 (86.0%) participants reported average-to-low knowledge of nirsevimab and the maternal vaccine, respectively, with differences across countries (p = 0.002). Despite limited knowledge, 311 (85.9%) pediatricians were willing to administer nirsevimab, and 319 (92.2%) supported its use for all infants. Nirsevimab administration's barriers, including unfamiliarity and logistical challenges, were cited by 69 (20.0%) pediatricians. Regarding immunization preferences, 165 (47.4%) pediatricians were very likely to support the maternal vaccine over nirsevimab. CONCLUSIONS: While pediatricians support RSV immunization, knowledge gaps and logistical barriers may hinder early-stage implementation. Optimizing education on RSV immunization will be crucial to improve uptake and prevention strategies.

This study evaluated pediatricians' knowledge, attitudes, and barriers to RSV immunization in Italy and Cyprus/Greece, where nirsevimab had not yet been implemented, and in Spain, where it was introduced in 2023/2024. A survey was distributed to pediatricians across Spain, Italy, and Cyprus/Greece in July-August/2024. Occupational characteristics, and knowledge, attitudes and practices toward palivizumab, nirsevimab, and the maternal vaccine were collected. Of 578 respondents (response rate = 19.3%), 50% were from Spain, 40% from Italy, and 10% from Cyprus/Greece. As 90% of responses came from Spain and Italy, the main analysis focused on these two countries. Descriptive and univariate analyses (Chi-square or Fisher's exact tests) were conducted. Respondents included pediatricians from community (51.7%), tertiary (30.4%), and primary/secondary care (17.9%) settings. Pediatricians were generally aware of RSV risk factors, without differences across countries. However, 245 (55.9%) and 375 (86.0%) participants reported average-to-low knowledge of nirsevimab and the maternal vaccine, respectively, with differences across countries (p = 0.002). Despite limited knowledge, 311 (85.9%) pediatricians were willing to administer nirsevimab, and 319 (92.2%) supported its use for all infants. Nirsevimab administration's barriers, including unfamiliarity and logistical challenges, were cited by 69 (20.0%) pediatricians. Regarding immunization preferences, 165 (47.4%) pediatricians were very likely to support the maternal vaccine over nirsevimab. While pediatricians support RSV immunization, knowledge gaps and logistical barriers may hinder early-stage implementation. Optimizing education on RSV immunization will be crucial to improve uptake and prevention strategies.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)免疫产品如尼塞韦单抗和孕妇疫苗接种等孕期预防策略是新推出的预防策略,但其实施需要了解儿科医生的知识和态度。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2024 年 7 月至 8 月,对西班牙、意大利和塞浦路斯/希腊的儿科医生进行了一项横断面调查,以评估对 RSV 免疫产品的知识、态度和障碍。
elements_zh.methods: 该调查收集了有关帕利珠单抗、尼塞韦单抗 和母亲 疫苗 的职业特征和知识、态度和实践数据,并使用卡方或 Fisher 精确检验进行描述性和单变量分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 在578名受访者中(应答率为19.3%),55.9%报告对尼塞韦单抗的知识水平为中等至较低,86.0%报告对母源尼塞韦单抗的知识水平为中等至较低,且不同国家间存在显著差异(p = 0.002)。尽管知识有限,85.9%的受访者愿意接种尼塞韦单抗,92.2%支持将其用于所有婴儿。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,虽然儿科医生支持 RSV 免疫接种,但知识差距和后勤障碍可能会阻碍早期实施,这凸显了有针对性的教育的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,优化 RSV 免疫教育对于改善接种和预防策略至关重要,特别是在新引入 尼塞韦单抗 的环境中。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 低答复率(19.3%)和地域不平衡(90%的答复来自西班牙和意大利)限制了普遍性,而且该研究依赖于自我报告的数据,这可能会引入偏差。

abstract_zh: 目的:尼塞韦单抗和孕期母体疫苗接种是新推出的针对呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)的预防策略。这项研究评估了意大利和塞浦路斯/希腊(尚未实施 尼塞韦单抗)以及西班牙(2023/2024 年引入 尼塞韦单抗)的儿科医生对 RSV 免疫的知识、态度和障碍。方法:2024 年 7 月至 8 月向西班牙、意大利和塞浦路斯/希腊的儿科医生分发了一项调查。收集职业特征以及对帕利珠单抗、尼塞韦单抗 和母亲 疫苗 的知识、态度和实践。在 578 名受访者中(回应率为 19.3%),50% 来自西班牙,40% 来自意大利,10% 来自塞浦路斯/希腊。由于90%的回复来自西班牙和意大利,因此主要分析集中在这两个国家。进行了描述性分析和单变量分析(卡方或费舍尔精确检验)。结果:受访者包括来自社区 (51.7%)、三级 (30.4%) 和初级/二级护理 (17.9%) 机构的儿科医生。儿科医生普遍了解 RSV 危险因素,各国之间没有差异。然而,分别有 245 名 (55.9%) 和 375 名 (86.0%) 参与者报告对 尼塞韦单抗 和母亲 疫苗 的了解处于平均至低水平,不同国家之间存在差异 (p = 0.002)。尽管知识有限,但 311 名 (85.9%) 儿科医生愿意使用 尼塞韦单抗,319 名 (92.2%) 名儿科医生支持对所有婴儿使用该药物。69 名 (20.0%) 儿科医生提到了 尼塞韦单抗 管理的障碍,包括不熟悉和后勤挑战。关于免疫偏好,165 名(47.4%)儿科医生很可能支持孕妇 疫苗 而不是 尼塞韦单抗。结论:虽然儿科医生支持 RSV 免疫接种,但知识差距和后勤障碍可能会阻碍早期实施。优化 RSV 免疫教育对于改善接种和预防策略至关重要。
