analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis in infants, focusing on the central question of whether tidal-breathing analysis (TBA) can objectively assess respiratory mechanics and bronchodilator responsiveness in acute bronchiolitis-like illness caused by RSV.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a case report and narrative synthesis without a systematic search or meta-analysis; it describes a single patient with severe RSV bronchiolitis-like illness and evaluates bronchodilator responsiveness using predefined TBA parameters before and after inhaled bronchodilator administration.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that TBA is feasible for identifying physiological bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness, with observed increases in time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF) and tPTEF/TE ratio, alongside decreases in expiratory time and total respiratory cycle duration, and increases in tidal volume and minute ventilation.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights uncertainty regarding whether TBA-defined bronchodilator responsiveness represents an early physiological marker of subsequent recurrent wheezing or asthma, noting that this hypothesis requires prospective validation in longitudinal studies.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine whether TBA-defined responsiveness can support individualized follow-up strategies and early identification of at-risk infants.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the use of tidal-breathing analysis (TBA) as a non-invasive bedside method to assess respiratory mechanics and bronchodilator responsiveness in infants with severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) bronchiolitis-like illness. A single case report demonstrates that TBA parameters, including time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF) and expiratory timing indices, improved following bronchodilator administration, suggesting a potential bronchodilator-responsive phenotype. However, the review emphasizes that these findings are preliminary and require validation in larger, prospective studies to determine whether TBA-defined responsiveness can predict long-term outcomes such as recurrent wheezing or asthma.

abstract_zh: 背景:急性 毛细支气管炎 是婴儿下呼吸道感染的最常见原因之一,并且仍然是一种临床异质综合征。目前的国际指南建议支持性治疗,通常不鼓励常规使用支气管扩张剂;然而,一部分患者可能有生理反应。潮汐呼吸分析 (TBA) 是一种非侵入性床边方法,用于客观评估呼吸力学,并且可以客观量化年龄较大儿童服用支气管扩张剂后的生理变化。病例介绍:我们报告了一名 23 个月大男孩的病例,该男孩患有严重的 RSV 毛细支气管炎 样喘息疾病,并发急性呼吸衰竭。在吸入支气管扩张剂给药前后,使用预定义的 TBA 参数评估支气管扩张剂反应性。治疗 后,患者达到潮气呼气流量峰值的时间 (tPTEF) 从 0.17 秒增加到 0.33 秒 (+94%),而他的 tPTEF/TE 比率从 0.12 增加到 0.27 (+125%)。呼气时间 (TE) 和总呼吸周期持续时间 (Ttot) 分别减少 12.6% 和 5.1%,而潮气量 (VT) 和每分钟通气量 (MV) 增加 12.1% 和 18.3%。呼气峰流量保持不变(支气管扩张剂给药前后均为 0.14 L/s)。讨论:据我们所知,这是使用床边 TBA 来表征严重 毛细支气管炎 类疾病的急性支气管扩张剂反应性的首批报告之一。呼气正时指数的改善,以及呼气峰值流量不变的情况下呼气时间的缩短,与支气管扩张剂给药后呼气流量动力学的改善一致。这些发现可以支持可能存在支气管扩张剂反应性生理表型的假设。先前的研究已证明婴儿期严重的 毛细支气管炎 与随后的复发性喘息或哮喘之间存在关联;然而,通过 TBA 客观测量的急性支气管扩张剂反应性是否表明这种表型代表了未来纵向研究的可检验假设。结论:该病例说明了床边 TBA 确定严重 毛细支气管炎 样疾病中生理性支气管扩张剂反应性的可行性。应进行前瞻性纵向研究,以确定 TBA 定义的反应性是否代表需要前瞻性验证的早期生理标志,以及这种生理分层是否可以支持个体化随访策略。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述检查了婴儿中的人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 毛细支气管炎,重点关注潮汐呼吸分析 (TBA) 是否可以客观评估 RSV 引起的急性 毛细支气管炎 样疾病的呼吸力学和支气管扩张剂反应性的核心问题。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该评论是 病例报告 和叙事综合,没有进行系统搜索或荟萃分析;它描述了一名患有严重 RSV 毛细支气管炎 样疾病的患者,并在吸入支气管扩张剂给药前后使用预定义的 TBA 参数评估支气管扩张剂反应性。

analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该综述表明,需要进行前瞻性纵向研究来确定 TBA 定义的反应性是否可以支持个体化随访策略和早期识别高危婴儿。

title: Epidemiology, temporal trends and co-infection of 13 respiratory pathogens in 32,125 children: a 3-year retrospective study
abstract: Background Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections bring heavy global disease burden. Clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features guides clinical management and public health prevention. Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients under 18 years receiving 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025. We extracted laboratory data and calculated pathogen positivity, single/co-infection proportions. Stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex and statistical collation of co-infection patterns were completed. Results In total, 32,125 children were included. The total pathogen positive rate reached 63.4%, including 49.8% single infection and 13.6% co-infection dominated by dual infection. Human rhinovirus (22.9%) ranked first, followed by respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%). Pathogens varied obviously across seasons and ages: HRV surged in spring and autumn; parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus prevailed in summer; syncytial virus and influenza peaked in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus mainly affected infants; rhinovirus and parainfluenza were prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers; Mycoplasma pneumoniae rose with age and peaked among school-age children. Dual infection occupied nearly all co-infections; the top non-influenza combinations were HRSV–HRV and HRV–HAdV. Infections with three or more pathogens were rare. Conclusions HRV and HRSV dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with obvious seasonal and age clustering. Most co-infections occurred in winter and young kids. HRV detection requires careful explanation for potential asymptomatic carriage. Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age-and seasonal-targeted diagnosis and targeted prevention including HRSV prevention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections impose a substantial global disease burden, and clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features is needed to guide clinical management and public health prevention.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study enrolled 32,125 patients under 18 years who underwent 13-pathogen multiplex PCR testing at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025.
analysis.methods: Laboratory data were extracted and analyzed to calculate pathogen positivity, single and co-infection proportions, with stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex.
analysis.main_results: The total pathogen positive rate was 63.4%, including 49.8% single infections and 13.6% co-infections, with dual infections comprising nearly all co-infections; human rhinovirus (22.9%) and respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%) were the most prevalent pathogens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors conclude that human rhinovirus and respiratory syncytial virus dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with clear seasonal and age-related clustering, highlighting the need for careful interpretation of rhinovirus detection due to potential asymptomatic carriage.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Local epidemiological patterns should inform age- and season-targeted diagnosis and prevention strategies, including targeted respiratory syncytial virus prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on multiplex PCR results, which may not distinguish asymptomatic carriage from active infection, reducing the certainty of causal inference.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed 32,125 children tested for 13 respiratory pathogens at a single Chinese hospital from 2023 to 2025. Overall, 63.4% were positive for at least one pathogen, with human rhinovirus (22.9%) and respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%) most common. Single infections accounted for 49.8% and co-infections for 13.6%, predominantly dual infections. Seasonal and age patterns were evident: rhinovirus peaked in spring and autumn, parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus in summer, and respiratory syncytial virus and influenza in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus primarily affected infants, while rhinovirus and parainfluenza were more prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers. The authors emphasize that local epidemiology should guide targeted diagnosis and prevention, including respiratory syncytial virus prevention, and caution that rhinovirus detection may reflect asymptomatic carriage.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 小儿急性呼吸道感染给全球带来了巨大的疾病负担,需要明确大流行后的流行病学特征来指导临床管理和公共卫生预防。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项回顾性研究纳入了 2023 年至 2025 年在华西第二大学医院接受 13 种病原体多重 PCR 检测的 32,125 名 18 岁以下患者。
elements_zh.methods: 提取并分析实验室数据,计算病原体阳性率、单一感染和合并感染比例,并按年份、季节、年龄和性别进行分层分析。
elements_zh.main_results: 病原菌总阳性率为63.4%,其中单一感染49.8%,合并感染13.6%,其中双重感染几乎全部是合并感染;人鼻病毒(22.9%)和呼吸道合胞病毒(15.2%)是最常见的病原体。

title_zh: 流行病学,32,125 名儿童中 13 种呼吸道病原体的时间趋势和合并感染:一项为期 3 年的回顾性研究
source_body_en: Background Pediatric acute respiratory tract infections bring heavy global disease burden. Clarifying post-pandemic epidemiological features guides clinical management and public health prevention. Methods This retrospective study enrolled patients under 18 years receiving 13-pathogen multiplex PCR at West China Second University Hospital from 2023 to 2025. We extracted laboratory data and calculated pathogen positivity, single/co-infection proportions. Stratified analyses by year, season, age and sex and statistical collation of co-infection patterns were completed. Results In total, 32,125 children were included. The total pathogen positive rate reached 63.4%, including 49.8% single infection and 13.6% co-infection dominated by dual infection. Human rhinovirus (22.9%) ranked first, followed by respiratory syncytial virus (15.2%). Pathogens varied obviously across seasons and ages: HRV surged in spring and autumn; parainfluenza, adenovirus and coronavirus prevailed in summer; syncytial virus and influenza peaked in winter. Respiratory syncytial virus mainly affected infants; rhinovirus and parainfluenza were prevalent in toddlers and preschoolers; Mycoplasma pneumoniae rose with age and peaked among school-age children. Dual infection occupied nearly all co-infections; the top non-influenza combinations were HRSV–HRV and HRV–HAdV. Infections with three or more pathogens were rare. Conclusions HRV and HRSV dominated pediatric respiratory pathogens with obvious seasonal and age clustering. Most co-infections occurred in winter and young kids. HRV detection requires careful explanation for potential asymptomatic carriage. Local epidemiological characteristics should inform age-and seasonal-targeted diagnosis and targeted prevention including HRSV prevention.

title: Late preterm and small for gestational age – double the risk?
abstract: Late preterm infants born after 34 + 0 and before 37 + 0 weeks of gestation account for more than 75% of all preterm births so any problems they may have represent a sizeable healthcare burden. It is increasingly recognised that they can suffer greater acute and chronic respiratory morbidity than infants born at term. In a single centre study of 1022 infants, the need for respiratory support was 32%,18% and 11% in infants born at 34, 35 and 36 weeks of gestational age respectively and for supplemental tube feeding was 55%, 24% and 8% respectively. 1 Amongst 1,650,450 infants born between 35 and 41 weeks of gestation between 1998 and 2016, the risks for respiratory, severe neonatal, infectious and neurological morbidities were highest at 35 weeks and gradually decreased until 39 weeks. 2 The results are influenced by ethnicity. In our single centre study Black late preterm infants less frequently needed invasive and non-invasive ventilation and had a shorter duration of length of stay (LOS). 3 Late preterm infants have a higher rate of readmission. 4 They have an increased risk of RSV infection and asthma at 18months and more wheeze and nocturnal cough at school age. 5 In a national cohort of 4,079,878 singletons born in Sweden between 1973 and 2013-4, of whom 14.9% were diagnosed with asthma, the late preterm individuals had 1.31 increased risk of asthma. 6 They also may have poorer lung function at follow-up, 7 particularly if exposed to passive smoking. At three to seven years those born late preterm had worse forced oscillometry results indicating increased peripheral airways resistance, particularly if they had been hospitalised for pulmonary infection and had passive smoke exposure.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the healthcare burden and morbidity associated with late preterm infants, who constitute over 75% of preterm births and face higher risks of respiratory complications compared to term infants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research synthesizes data from multiple cohorts, including a national cohort of 1,650,450 infants born between 35 and 41 weeks of gestation from 1998 to 2016, and a Swedish cohort of 4,079,878 singletons born between 1973 and 2013-4.
analysis.methods: The study analyzed morbidity risks across gestational ages using population-level datasets, with outcomes stratified by gestational week and adjusted for factors such as ethnicity.
analysis.main_results: Risks for respiratory, severe neonatal, infectious, and neurological morbidities were highest at 35 weeks of gestation and gradually decreased until 39 weeks. Late preterm infants had a 1.31 increased risk of asthma compared to term infants.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight that late preterm birth is associated with elevated risks of respiratory and neurological morbidities, including asthma, with the highest burden observed at 35 weeks of gestation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results underscore the need for targeted surveillance and preventive strategies for late preterm infants, particularly those born at 35 weeks, to mitigate long-term respiratory and neurological complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited by single-centre data for some analyses and potential confounding by ethnicity and passive smoke exposure, warranting cautious interpretation of the findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the morbidity risks associated with late preterm birth, defined as delivery between 34 + 0 and 37 + 0 weeks of gestation. Using population-level data from over 1.65 million infants born between 1998 and 2016, the authors report that risks for respiratory, severe neonatal, infectious, and neurological morbidities are highest at 35 weeks of gestation and decline with advancing gestational age. In a Swedish cohort of nearly 4.1 million singletons, late preterm infants exhibited a 1.31-fold increased risk of asthma compared to term infants. The findings emphasize the substantial healthcare burden of late preterm birth and highlight the need for targeted interventions to address respiratory and neurological complications in this vulnerable population.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究综合了多个 队列研究 的数据,其中包括 1998 年至 2016 年期间出生的 1,650,450 名妊娠 35 至 41 周之间出生的婴儿的全国 队列研究,以及 1973 年至 2013-4 年间出生的 4,079,878 名瑞典 队列研究 的数据。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用人口水平数据集分析了不同孕龄的发病风险,结果按孕周分层,并根据种族等因素进行调整。
elements_zh.main_results: 呼吸道疾病、严重新生儿疾病、感染性疾病和神经系统疾病的风险在妊娠 35 周时最高,并逐渐下降,直至 39 周。与足月儿相比,晚期早产儿患哮喘的风险增加 1.31。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果强调,晚期早产与呼吸系统和神经系统疾病(包括哮喘)风险升高相关,其中在妊娠 35 周时观察到的负担最高。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调,晚期早产儿(特别是 35 周出生的早产儿)需要有针对性的 监测 和预防策略,以减轻长期呼吸和神经并发症。

title: Five-year surveillance of pediatric respiratory pathogens in Fuzhou (2019–2024): impact of the COVID-19 pandemic
abstract: This study aims to investigate the epidemiological characteristics and distribution patterns of respiratory pathogens in children in Fuzhou between 2019 and 2024, with a particular focus on changes associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. This retrospective study included children aged 0–18 years hospitalized for acute respiratory infections in Fuzhou Children’s Hospital of Fujian Province between June 2019 and May 2024. Nasal swab specimens were collected to test for 11 respiratory pathogens using multiplex PCR. The distribution characteristics of pathogens were analyzed across age groups, genders, seasons, and pandemic phases. A total of 37,724 nasal swab specimens were included, comprising 22,327 males and 15,397 females. The overall test positivity rate was 58.78%. Rhinovirus had the highest positivity rate (20.95%), followed by respiratory syncytial virus (11.12%) and Mycoplasma pneumoniae (6.89%). Co-infections were identified in 8.08% of specimens. Multivariable logistic regression revealed distinct age, sex, and seasonal patterns for the three most common pathogens: M. pneumoniae risk increased progressively with age (≥ 6 years: OR = 6.100), RSV predominated in infants, and rhinovirus showed a less pronounced age pattern. Across four pandemic phases (pre-pandemic, strict NPIs, transition, and post-restriction), pathogen detection exhibited distinct trajectories. pneumoniae dropped sharply during the pandemic period and resurged post-restriction (from 1.11% to 12.61%); rhinovirus declined during strict NPIs but rebounded quickly and remained stable; RSV paradoxically increased during strict NPIs (from 10.66% to 26.74%). This study provides evidence on pediatric respiratory pathogen epidemiology in Fuzhou, revealing pathogen-specific changes in detection patterns across different pandemic phases. These findings underscore the importance of continued surveillance and pathogen-targeted prevention strategies in the post-pandemic era.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the need to understand how the COVID-19 pandemic altered the epidemiology of pediatric respiratory pathogens in Fuzhou, focusing on pathogen-specific changes and gaps in knowledge about their distribution patterns in children.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective study enrolled 37,724 children aged 0–18 years hospitalized for acute respiratory infections at Fuzhou Children’s Hospital between June 2019 and May 2024, including 22,327 males and 15,397 females.
analysis.methods: Nasal swab specimens were tested for 11 respiratory pathogens using multiplex PCR, and multivariable logistic regression was applied to analyze age, sex, and seasonal patterns for the most common pathogens.
analysis.main_results: RSV positivity was 11.12% overall, with multivariable analysis showing RSV predominance in infants; RSV detection paradoxically increased during strict non-pharmaceutical interventions (from 10.66% to 26.74%) and declined post-restriction.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted RSV’s atypical rise during strict NPIs as a potential consequence of reduced early-life exposure leading to delayed infections, highlighting pathogen-specific pandemic effects not previously detailed in Fuzhou.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support targeted RSV surveillance and prevention strategies in the post-pandemic era, particularly for infants who remain at highest risk during atypical circulation periods.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s single-center retrospective design and reliance on hospital-based sampling limit generalizability to community settings, warranting cautious interpretation of RSV-specific trends.

analysis.summary_en: This five-year retrospective study in Fuzhou analyzed 37,724 pediatric respiratory specimens using multiplex PCR to assess changes in pathogen detection across pandemic phases. RSV was detected in 11.12% of cases, with multivariable analysis confirming its predominance in infants. Notably, RSV positivity paradoxically increased during strict non-pharmaceutical interventions (from 10.66% to 26.74%) before declining post-restriction, suggesting pandemic-related shifts in transmission dynamics. Rhinovirus remained the most frequently detected pathogen overall. The authors propose that reduced early-life exposure during NPIs may have delayed RSV infections, underscoring the need for continued surveillance and targeted prevention in the post-pandemic period. However, as a single-center study, findings may not reflect community-level trends.

abstract_zh: 本研究旨在调查2019年至2024年福州市儿童呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征和分布模式,特别关注与COVID-19大流行相关的变化。这项回顾性研究纳入了2019年6月至2024年5月期间在福建省福州儿童医院因急性呼吸道感染住院的0-18岁儿童。收集鼻拭子标本,采用多重PCR检测11种呼吸道病原体。分析病原体在年龄组、性别、季节和流行阶段的分布特征。共纳入37,724份鼻拭子样本,其中男性22,327人,女性15,397人。总体检测阳性率为58.78%。鼻病毒阳性率最高(20.95%),其次是呼吸道合胞病毒(11.12%)和肺炎支原体(6.89%)。8.08% 的标本中发现了双重感染。多变量逻辑回归揭示了三种最常见病原体的不同年龄、性别和季节模式:肺炎支原体风险随着年龄的增长而逐渐增加(≥ 6 岁:OR = 6.100),RSV 在婴儿中占主导地位,而鼻病毒则表现出不太明显的年龄模式。在四个大流行阶段(大流行前、严格的 NPI、过渡和限制后),病原体检测表现出不同的轨迹。肺炎疫情期间大幅下降,限购后回升(从1.11%上升至12.61%);鼻病毒在严格的 NPI 期间有所下降,但迅速反弹并保持稳定;在严格的 NPI 期间,RSV 反而增加(从 10.66% 增加到 26.74%)。这项研究提供了福州儿童呼吸道病原体 流行病学 的证据,揭示了不同流行阶段检测模式的病原体特异性变化。这些发现强调了大流行后时代持续的 监测 和针对病原体的预防策略的重要性。

title: Bayesian epidemic alignment for causal evaluation of seasonal infectious-disease interventions
abstract: Seasonal infectious-disease interventions are commonly evaluated with interrupted time-series or pre--post designs that align epidemics by calendar week. When epidemic onset, speed or peak timing differs between seasons, such comparisons confound a shift in epidemic phase with a change in disease burden. We propose a Bayesian causal count model in which season-specific affine transformations map calendar time to a latent epidemic clock, and intervention effects are estimated on that clock rather than on the calendar. The alignment is a model component rather than a preprocessing step, so uncertainty about epidemic timing propagates into every causal contrast. The model uses a negative-binomial observation distribution, hierarchical area, season and area-season effects, a shrunk Fourier epidemic curve, and a continuous programme-intensity exposure. Posterior g-computation yields prevented cases, prevented fractions, peak attenuation and epidemic displacement, under both a controlled contrast and a dynamic contrast that propagates disease history within each arm. A two-tier simulation study evaluates bias, root mean squared error, interval coverage and parameter recovery under stable timing, epidemic-clock variation, intensity-dependent ascertainment and area-level confounding. We illustrate the framework using open Catalan primary-care surveillance and respiratory syncytial virus immunisation data, with explicit attention to the overlap in programme intensity that identifies the effect.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a Bayesian causal count model to evaluate seasonal infectious-disease interventions, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The model aligns epidemics using a latent epidemic clock rather than calendar time, allowing uncertainty in timing to propagate into causal contrasts. It uses a negative-binomial distribution and hierarchical effects to estimate intervention impacts, including prevented cases and peak attenuation. The framework is demonstrated using Catalan primary-care surveillance and RSV immunisation data, highlighting the importance of programme intensity overlap in identifying effects. A simulation study assesses the model's performance under various conditions, providing moderate evidence for its validity. The approach offers new insights into causal evaluation by addressing limitations of traditional pre-post designs, which can confound changes in epidemic timing with shifts in disease burden. This could improve surveillance and intervention strategies for RSV, particularly in settings with overlapping programme intensity and epidemic patterns.

title: Rabeprazole exhibits broad-spectrum fusion inhibition against Nipah pseudovirus and authentic HCoV-OC43 and RSV
abstract: Rabeprazole was previously defined as a small-molecule fusion inhibitor that binds the conserved hydrophobic HR1 groove of the SARS-CoV-2 spike and blocks six-helix bundle assembly. Here, we expand its antiviral spectrum and demonstrate potent activity against Nipah virus pseudotype, HCoV-229E, and RSV. Using SPR, pseudovirus neutralization, docking, and 100-ns MD simulations, we validated binding of Rabeprazole to the HR1 domains of NiV F glycoprotein and HCoV-229E spike, with a conserved fusion-inhibitory mechanism. Systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) profiling among clinically approved PPIs revealed that Ilaprazole and Lansoprazole exhibited stronger anti-NiV potency than Rabeprazole, while Rabeprazole sulfide showed enhanced antiviral activity relative to the parent compound. Rabeprazole also inhibited live RSV and HCoV-229E infection in a dose-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings establish the HR1 groove as a druggable pan-viral target and validate benzimidazole-based PPIs as a versatile scaffold for developing orally available, broad-spectrum antivirals against phylogenetically distinct enveloped viruses that rely on class I fusion machinery.

Using SPR, pseudovirus neutralization, docking, and 100-ns MD simulations, we validated binding of Rabeprazole to the HR1 domains of NiV F glycoprotein and HCoV-229E spike, with a conserved fusion-inhibitory mechanism. Systematic structure-activity relationship (SAR) profiling among clinically approved PPIs revealed that Ilaprazole and Lansoprazole exhibited stronger anti-NiV potency than Rabeprazole, while Rabeprazole sulfide showed enhanced antiviral activity relative to the parent compound. Rabeprazole also inhibited live RSV and HCoV-229E infection in a dose-dependent manner. Collectively, these findings establish the HR1 groove as a druggable pan-viral target and validate benzimidazole-based PPIs as a versatile scaffold for developing orally available, broad-spectrum antivirals against phylogenetically distinct enveloped viruses that rely on class I fusion machinery.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to expand the antiviral spectrum of Rabeprazole, a known SARS-CoV-2 fusion inhibitor, to include Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and other enveloped viruses. The research was motivated by the need for broad-spectrum antivirals against phylogenetically distinct viruses that rely on class I fusion machinery.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using a combination of pseudovirus neutralization, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. It involved testing Rabeprazole against RSV and other related viruses, with a focus on its mechanism of action and antiviral potency.
analysis.methods: The researchers employed SPR (Surface Plasmon Resonance), pseudovirus neutralization assays, molecular docking simulations, and 100-ns MD (Molecular Dynamics) simulations to validate the binding of Rabeprazole to the HR1 domains of NiV F glycoprotein and HCoV-229E spike, and to assess its antiviral activity.
analysis.main_results: Systematic SAR (Structure-Activity Relationship) profiling among clinically approved PPIs showed that Ilaprazole and Lansoprazole had stronger anti-NiV potency than Rabeprazole, while Rabeprazole sulfide demonstrated enhanced antiviral activity compared to the parent compound. Rabeprazole also inhibited live RSV and HCoV-229E infection in a dose-dependent manner.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Rabeprazole and its derivatives can inhibit RSV and other enveloped viruses through a conserved fusion-inhibitory mechanism, highlighting the HR1 groove as a potential druggable target for broad-spectrum antivirals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results provide a foundation for developing orally available, broad-spectrum antivirals targeting the HR1 groove, which could be valuable for combating RSV and related viruses that cause respiratory infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro and pseudovirus assays, and the evidence strength is moderate due to the lack of in vivo testing and clinical trials. The findings are based on structure-activity relationships and computational models, which may not fully reflect real-world efficacy.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the antiviral potential of Rabeprazole against Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) and other enveloped viruses. The research expands on Rabeprazole's known role as a SARS-CoV-2 fusion inhibitor by demonstrating its activity against RSV and HCoV-229E. Using SPR, pseudovirus neutralization, molecular docking, and MD simulations, the study validates Rabeprazole's binding to HR1 domains and its dose-dependent inhibition of live RSV and HCoV-229E. The findings suggest that the HR1 groove is a viable target for broad-spectrum antivirals, with implications for developing new therapeutic strategies. However, the study's reliance on in vitro and computational methods limits its evidence strength, which is assessed as moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在扩大雷贝拉唑(一种已知的 SARS-CoV-2 融合抑制剂)的 抗病毒药物 谱,以包括 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和其他包膜病毒。这项研究的动机是需要广谱 抗病毒药物 来对抗依赖 I 类融合机制的系统发育独特的病毒。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究结合了假病毒中和、分子对接和分子动力学模拟进行。它涉及测试雷贝拉唑针对 RSV 和其他相关病毒的作用,重点是其作用机制和 抗病毒药物 效力。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员采用SPR(表面等离子体共振)、假病毒中和试验、分子对接模拟和100纳秒MD(分子动力学)模拟来验证雷贝拉唑与NiV F糖蛋白和HCoV-229E刺突的HR1结构域的结合,并评估其抗病毒药物活性。
elements_zh.main_results: 临床批准的 PPI 的系统 SAR(结构-活性关系)分析表明,艾普拉唑和兰索拉唑比雷贝拉唑具有更强的抗 NiV 效力,而与母体化合物相比,硫化雷贝拉唑表现出增强的 抗病毒药物 活性。雷贝拉唑还以剂量依赖性方式抑制活 RSV 和 HCoV-229E 感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,雷贝拉唑及其衍生物可以通过保守的融合抑制机制抑制 RSV 和其他包膜病毒,强调 HR1 沟作为广谱 抗病毒药物 的潜在药物靶点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果为开发针对 HR1 沟的口服广谱 抗病毒药物 奠定了基础,这对于对抗引起呼吸道感染的 RSV 和相关病毒可能有价值。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究仅限于体外和假病毒检测,由于缺乏体内测试和临床试验,证据强度中等。这些发现基于结构-活动关系和计算模型,可能无法完全反映现实世界的功效。

abstract_zh: 雷贝拉唑此前被定义为一种小分子融合抑制剂,可结合 SARS-CoV-2 刺突的保守疏水性 HR1 凹槽并阻断六螺旋束组装。在这里,我们扩展了其 抗病毒药物 谱,并证明了其对尼帕病毒假型、HCoV-229E 和 RSV 的有效活性。使用 SPR、假病毒中和、对接和 100 ns MD 模拟,我们验证了雷贝拉唑与 NiV F 糖蛋白和 HCoV-229E 刺突的 HR1 结构域的结合,并具有保守的融合抑制机制。临床批准的 PPI 的系统构效关系 (SAR) 分析显示,艾普拉唑和兰索拉唑比雷贝拉唑表现出更强的抗 NiV 效力,而雷贝拉唑硫化物相对于母体化合物表现出增强的 抗病毒药物 活性。雷贝拉唑还以剂量依赖性方式抑制活 RSV 和 HCoV-229E 感染。总的来说,这些发现将 HR1 沟确立为可药物化的泛病毒靶标,并验证基于苯并咪唑的 PPI 作为通用支架,可用于开发口服广谱 抗病毒药物,对抗依赖于 I 类融合机制的系统发育独特的包膜病毒。

E-mail: hisa1988@fmu.ac.jp Accepted Manuscript 2 Abstract Papiliotrema laurentii is an environmental yeast that has been increasingly recognized as a cause of invasive infections, particularly in individuals with impaired cellular immunity. However, reports in Japan are limited. We describe a rare case of bloodstream infection caused by Papiliotrema laurentii in a 4-year-old Japanese girl with cerebral palsy and epilepsy. She was diagnosed with respiratory syncytial virus- associated acute encephalopathy, and received methylprednisolone pulse therapy as part of intensive management. Despite completion of the 3-day steroid therapy, her fever persisted. Subsequent blood cultures performed 3 days after steroid therapy completion revealed the presence of yeast-like organisms. The isolate was identified as Papiliotrema laurentii using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 regions. Antifungal susceptibility testing revealed a characteristic profile distinct from that of common yeasts. Micafungin was switched to liposomal amphotericin B and later to fosfluconazole, resulting in complete resolution. The patient remained relapse-free at the 6-month follow-up. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of Papiliotrema laurentii fungemia in Japan; however, its true incidence may be underestimated because of diagnostic limitations and limited surveillance data. This case suggests that methylprednisolone pulse therapy may predispose even immunocompetent children to opportunistic fungemia and that accurate identification and susceptibility testing are essential for appropriate antifungal management. Keywords: Acute encephalopathy; Antifungal susceptibility; Cryptococcus laurentii; Fungemia; Papiliotrema laurentii Accepted Manuscript 3 Introduction Papiliotrema laurentii (formerly Cryptococcus laurentii) has been increasingly recognized as a cause of invasive infections worldwide (Khawcharoenporn et al. 2007; Arendrup et al. 2014). Its antifungal susceptibility patterns differ from those of more common yeast pathogens (Pfaller et al. 2009; Bernal-Martinez et al. 2010). This environmental yeast is distributed globally (Mattsson et al. 1999; Filion et al. 2006; Andrade-Silva et al. 2010), including in East Asia (Jang et al. 2011), and often causes invasive diseases, primarily in individuals with impaired cellular immunity (Manfredi et al. 2006). Despite its widespread environmental presence, reports of P. laurentii infection in Japan are extremely scarce. To date, only a single case of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis has been described (Asano et al. 2015), suggesting that invasive P. laurentii infections may be underdiagnosed in Japan. Methylprednisolone pulse therapy is commonly used in Japan for acute encephalopathy, according to the hypothesis that excessive inflammatory responses contribute to neurological injury (Omata and Takanashi 2025). However, the therapeutic efficacy of corticosteroids remains controversial; although they may be effective in the treatment of encephalopathy associated with hypercytokinemia (Okumura et al. 2009), their benefits for other pathological conditions have not been established (Hayashi et al. 2012). Because high-dose corticosteroids can transiently suppress cellular immunity, careful attention to the risk of opportunistic infections is warranted. Glucocorticoids exert immunosuppressive effects through multiple mechanisms, including inhibition of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling and proinflammatory cytokine production, reduced antigen presentation by dendritic cells, impaired monocyte–macrophage and T-cell Accepted Manuscript 4 function, and modulation of innate immune responses through epigenetic reprogramming and disruption of trained immunity. Collectively, these effects increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections (Cain and Cidlowski 2017). Herein, we report the first pediatric case of P. laurentii bloodstream infection, also known as fungemia, in Japan following methylprednisolone pulse therapy for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated acute encephalopathy. Informed consent for publication of this case report was obtained from the patient’s guardians. Case Presentation A 4-year-old Japanese girl with a history of severe neonatal asphyxia, hypoxic– ischemic encephalopathy, symptomatic epilepsy, status epilepticus associated with coronavirus disease 2019, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted to a local hospital for febrile seizures. Seizures were controlled with midazolam and thiopental; however, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging revealed hyperintense lesions in the occipital lobes (Fig. 1A), with no corresponding signal changes on T2-weighted imaging/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery imaging (Fig. 1B). A rapid antigen test was positive for RSV, and she was diagnosed with RSV-associated acute encephalopathy before transfer to our tertiary care center. On admission, the neurological status of the patient was severely impaired, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of E1V2M4. Pupils measured 2.5 mm bilaterally, with intact light reflexes. She was febrile (38.8°C) and hemodynamically unstable, with a heart rate of 110 beats/min, blood pressure of 79/52 mmHg, prolonged capillary refill time of 4 s, and peripheral coldness. Respiratory findings included glossoptosis, diminished Accepted Manuscript 5 breathing sounds, and intercostal retractions. Initial laboratory evaluation showed elevated inflammatory markers: white blood cell count, 8,600/μL; C-reactive protein level, 3.05 mg/dL; aspartate aminotransferase level, 215 U/L; alanine aminotransferase level, 58 U/L; and procalcitonin level, 23.61 ng/mL. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed no pleocytosis, with protein 16 mg/dL and glucose 65 mg/dL. Gram staining and culture results were negative (Table 1). Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of nasal discharge, sputum, whole blood, serum, and cerebrospinal fluid yielded negative results for herpes simplex virus 1/2 and human herpesvirus 6. Human herpesvirus 7 (HHV-7) was detected in aspirated sputum (1.66E+03 copies /mL) and whole blood (9.13E+03 copies /mL). In addition, reverse transcription PCR (RT-PCR) identified RSV subtype A in nasopharyngeal swab (5.36E+09 copies /mL) and aspirated sputum (5.37E+09 copies /mL) specimens (Supplementary Table S1). Primers and probes used for the PCR and RT-PCR assays were those previously reported (Okabe et al. 2025). Electroencephalography demonstrated suppressed background activity attributable to sedative medications (Fig. 2). Chest radiography revealed atelectasis of the left upper lobe (Fig. 3), which contributed to the diagnosis of aspiration pneumonia. The patient was ultimately diagnosed with RSV-associated acute encephalopathy and acute pneumonia. She was intubated, mechanically ventilated, and managed in the pediatric intensive care unit. A central venous catheter was placed in the right femoral vein to secure a route for the administration of vasoactive agents. Normothermia therapy using an Arctic Sun device and methylprednisolone pulse therapy (30 mg/kg/day) were initiated. Mitochondrial cocktail therapy (ascorbic acid, benfotiamine, pyridoxine, Accepted Manuscript 6 cyanocobalamin, and carnitine) was also administered to support mitochondrial function in the context of possible metabolic encephalopathy (Omata and Takanashi 2025). Ampicillin/sulbactam (150 mg/kg/day) was administered to treat suspected aspiration pneumonia. Dopamine treatment was initiated to treat sedation-related hypotension. Methylprednisolone pulse therapy was administered for 3 days. Although active temperature management was stopped on day 4, the fever persisted. Oliguria developed on day 6, necessitating escalation of dopamine levels. On day 7, the central venous catheter was removed, and blood cultures were obtained. The fever resolved, and antibiotics were discontinued on day 10. After 80 h of incubation, yeast-like organisms were detected in one anaerobic blood culture bottle obtained via peripheral venipuncture (Fig. 4), whereas the catheter tip culture was negative. Candidemia was suspected based on the detection of yeast-like organisms in blood culture, and micafungin (2 mg/kg/day), a first-line empirical therapy for candidemia, was initiated on day 11. The patient was extubated on the same day that her respiratory status improved. On day 14, the isolate was identified as P. laurentii by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry, with a confidence score of >2.0. Identification was confirmed by sequencing the internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 regions, which showed 100% similarity with the reference sequence (GenBank accession no. KY108740.1). Subsequently, treatment was switched to liposomal amphotericin B (3 mg/kg/day). On day 35, antifungal susceptibility testing was performed according to the Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute standard M27 (4th edition) (CLSI 2017). Testing revealed characteristic minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs): micafungin, > 16 mg/L; amphotericin B, 1 mg/L; and fluconazole, 4 mg/L (Table 2). Consequently, Accepted Manuscript 7 therapy was de-escalated to fosfluconazole (5 mg/kg/day). Although clinical breakpoints have not been established for P. laurentii, the MIC values for amphotericin B and fluconazole were within the epidemiological cutoff values reported for Cryptococcus neoformans (Espinel-Ingroff et al. 2012). Antifungal treatment (liposomal amphotericin B and fosfluconazole) was continued for 28 days. Follow-up blood cultures obtained on days 11, 12, 14, and 22 were negative. Ophthalmologic examinations were performed on days 14, 21, and 28, and none of them revealed any evidence of endophthalmitis. The clinical course, including the timing of microbiological identification and antifungal treatment modification, is summarized in Figure 5. Considering steroid-related temporal immunosuppression, antifungal consolidation therapy was not administered. The patient was subsequently diagnosed with laryngomalacia and underwent tracheostomy. She was discharged from the pediatric intensive care unit on day 67 and transferred back to the referring hospital on day 78. She remained relapse-free at the 6-month follow-up. Discussion A salient feature of this case was the development of P. laurentii fungemia after methylprednisolone pulse therapy for RSV-associated acute encephalopathy. Blood cultures were positive for P. laurentii, confirming a diagnosis of fungemia. Based on antifungal susceptibility testing, we tailored the antifungal therapy to agents with expected activity against the isolate, resulting in successful treatment without relapse. This case report highlights two important clinical findings. First, P. laurentii fungemia, with atypical antifungal susceptibility patterns, can occur in Japan and should Accepted Manuscript 8 be considered in cases of bloodstream yeast infections. Second, methylprednisolone pulse therapy for acute encephalopathy may have been associated with the development of an opportunistic fungal infection in this case. P. laurentii fungemia has been reported in neonates (Cheng et al. 2001; Al-Otaibi et al. 2021; Gupta et al. 2018; Johnson et al. 1998), patients receiving chemotherapy (Londero et al. 2019), individuals with glomerulonephritis treated with corticosteroids (Furman-Kuklińska et al. 2009), and hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients (Park et al. 2017; Krcméry et al. 1997). To the best of our knowledge, this is the first reported case of P. laurentii fungemia complicating RSV-associated acute encephalopathy ever reported. Although this is the first reported case of P. laurentii fungemia in Japan, the apparent rarity may reflect underdiagnosis rather than true absence. P. laurentii can be misidentified as other yeast species using conventional diagnostic methods, and routine surveillance data for non-neoformans Cryptococcus species are limited. Therefore, the true incidence of P. laurentii infection in Japan may be underestimated. P. laurentii has been isolated from environmental samples including bird droppings, soil, and tree hollows in various geographic regions (Mattsson et al. 1999; Andrade-Silva et al. 2010; Jang et al. 2011; Sláviková and Vadkertiová 2003; Prakash et al. 2018). Notably, our patient had no history of exposure to birds or other environmental risk factors. This observation raises the hypothesis that P. laurentii is present in the general environment in Japan and can cause infection under conditions of transient immunosuppression. Although the patient had no underlying primary immunodeficiency, she was exposed to risk factors for fungemia, including transient impairment of cellular immunity induced by methylprednisolone pulse therapy and the presence of a central venous catheter (Khawcharoenporn et al. 2007). In addition, severe RSV infection, Accepted Manuscript 9 critical illness, immune dysregulation associated with systemic inflammation, and prolonged pediatric intensive care unit exposure may also have contributed to increased susceptibility to opportunistic fungal infection. Although the catheter tip culture was negative, the possibility that femoral venous catheterization contributed to fungal invasion cannot be excluded. Previous reports have shown that P. laurentii generally exhibits susceptibility to amphotericin B, whereas susceptibility to azoles is variable and echinocandins have limited activity (Pfaller et al. 2009; Bernal-Martinez et al. 2010). The limited activity of echinocandins against Cryptococcus species has been attributed to intrinsic resistance mechanisms despite the presence of β-1,3-D-glucan synthase as the antifungal target (Chen et al. 2011). These findings highlight the importance of accurate species identification for appropriate antifungal selection. HHV-7 was detected in this case, although its clinical significance remains uncertain. Herpes virus has been reported to modulate host immune responses, particularly affecting T-cell function, and may contribute to transient immunosuppression (Alibek et al. 2014). Although HHV-7 was detected in sputum and whole blood samples, the HHV-7 DNA level was low and HHV-7 was not detected in serum. On the basis of these findings, RSV was considered the primary etiological agent in this case. However, HHV-7 detection may represent viral reactivation, incidental detection, or a potential contributor to the encephalopathic presentation, and these possibilities cannot be excluded. A limitation of this report is that the antifungal susceptibility of P. laurentii was interpreted with reference to epidemiological cutoff values for C. neoformans. Although these species are phylogenetically related, differences in susceptibility profiles across species may limit the validity of this extrapolation. Accepted Manuscript 10 In conclusion, we report the first case of P. laurentii fungemia in Japan that occurred after methylprednisolone pulse therapy for RSV-associated acute encephalopathy. Clinicians should recognize that P. laurentii has a unique antifungal susceptibility profile and that high-dose corticosteroid therapy may increase the risk of fungemia, even in children without chronic immunodeficiency. This case highlights the importance of considering opportunistic fungal infections and performing early fungal surveillance in patients with persistent fever following immunosuppressive therapy. In addition, advanced diagnostic tools such as matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and molecular sequencing may facilitate accurate identification of rare pathogens and guide appropriate antifungal therapy. Careful risk– benefit assessment of methylprednisolone pulse therapy and vigilance for opportunistic infections are essential when managing persistent fever after immunosuppressive therapy. E-mail: hisa1988@fmu.ac.jp Accepted Manuscript 2 Abstract Papiliotrema laurentii is an environmental yeast that has been increasingly recognized as a cause of invasive infections, particularly in individuals with impaired cellular immunity. However, reports in Japan are limited. We describe a rare case of bloodstream infection caused by Papiliotrema laurentii in a 4-year-old Japanese girl with cerebral palsy and epilepsy. She was diagnosed with respiratory syncytial virus- associated acute encephalopathy, and received methylprednisolone pulse therapy as part of intensive management. Despite completion of the 3-day steroid therapy, her fever persisted. Subsequent blood cultures performed 3 days after steroid therapy completion revealed the presence of yeast-like organisms. The isolate was identified as Papiliotrema laurentii using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry and sequencing of the internal transcribed spacer and D1/D2 regions. Antifungal susceptibility testing revealed a characteristic profile distinct from that of common yeasts. Micafungin was switched to liposomal amphotericin B and later to fosfluconazole, resulting in complete resolution. The patient remained relapse-free at the 6-month follow-up. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of Papiliotrema laurentii fungemia in Japan; however, its true incidence may be underestimated because of diagnostic limitations and limited surveillance data. This case suggests that methylprednisolone pulse therapy may predispose even immunocompetent children to opportunistic fungemia and that accurate identification and susceptibility testing are essential for appropriate antifungal management. Keywords: Acute encephalopathy; Antifungal susceptibility; Cryptococcus laurentii; Fungemia; Papiliotrema laurentii Accepted Manuscript 3 Introduction Papiliotrema laurentii (formerly Cryptococcus laurentii) has been increasingly recognized as a cause of invasive infections worldwide (Khawcharoenporn et al. 2007; Arendrup et al. 2014). Its antifungal susceptibility patterns differ from those of more common yeast pathogens (Pfaller et al. 2009; Bernal-Martinez et al. 2010). This environmental yeast is distributed globally (Mattsson et al. 1999; Filion et al. 2006; Andrade-Silva et al. 2010), including in East Asia (Jang et al. 2011), and often causes invasive diseases, primarily in individuals with impaired cellular immunity (Manfredi et al. 2006). Despite its widespread environmental presence, reports of P. laurentii infection in Japan are extremely scarce. To date, only a single case of peritoneal dialysis-associated peritonitis has been described (Asano et al. 2015), suggesting that invasive P. laurentii infections may be underdiagnosed in Japan. Methylprednisolone pulse therapy is commonly used in Japan for acute encephalopathy, according to the hypothesis that excessive inflammatory responses contribute to neurological injury (Omata and Takanashi 2025). However, the therapeutic efficacy of corticosteroids remains controversial; although they may be effective in the treatment of encephalopathy associated with hypercytokinemia (Okumura et al. 2009), their benefits for other pathological conditions have not been established (Hayashi et al. 2012). Because high-dose corticosteroids can transiently suppress cellular immunity, careful attention to the risk of opportunistic infections is warranted. Glucocorticoids exert immunosuppressive effects through multiple mechanisms, including inhibition of nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB) signaling and proinflammatory cytokine production, reduced antigen presentation by dendritic cells, impaired monocyte–macrophage and T-cell Accepted Manuscript 4 function, and modulation of innate immune responses through epigenetic reprogramming and disruption of trained immunity. Collectively, these effects increase susceptibility to opportunistic infections (Cain and Cidlowski 2017). Herein, we report the first pediatric case of P. laurentii bloodstream infection, also known as fungemia, in Japan following methylprednisolone pulse therapy for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated acute encephalopathy. Informed consent for publication of this case report was obtained from the patient’s guardians. Case Presentation A 4-year-old Japanese girl with a history of severe neonatal asphyxia, hypoxic– ischemic encephalopathy, symptomatic epilepsy, status epilepticus associated with coronavirus disease 2019, and gastrostomy dependence was admitted to a local hospital for febrile seizures. Seizures were controlled with midazolam and thiopental; however, diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging revealed hyperintense lesions in the occipital lobes (Fig. 1A), with no corresponding signal changes on T2-weighted imaging/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery imaging (Fig. 1B). A rapid antigen test was positive for RSV, and she was diagnosed with RSV-associated acute encephalopathy before transfer to our tertiary care center. On admission, the neurological status of the patient was severely impaired, with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of E1V2M4. Pupils measured 2.5 mm bilaterally, with intact light reflexes. She was febrile (38.8°C) and hemodynamically unstable, with a heart rate of 110 beats/min, blood pressure of 79/52 mmHg, prolonged capillary refill time of 4 s, and peripheral coldness. Respiratory findings included glossoptosis, diminished Accepted Manuscript 5 breathing sounds, and intercostal retractions. Initial laboratory evaluation showed elevated inflammatory markers: white blood cell count, 8,600/μL; C-reactive protein level, 3.05 mg/dL; aspartate aminotransferase level, 215 U/L; alanine aminotransferase level, 58 U/L; and procalcitonin level, 23.61 ng/mL. Cerebrospinal fluid analysis revealed no pleocytosis, with protein 16 mg/dL and glucose 65 mg/dL. Gram staining and culture results were negative (Table 1). Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing of nasal discharge, sputum, whole blood, serum, and cerebrospinal fluid yielded negative results for herpes simplex virus 1/2 and human herpesvirus 6. analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 4-year-old Japanese girl with cerebral palsy and epilepsy who developed Papiliotrema laurentii bloodstream infection following methylprednisolone pulse therapy for respiratory syncytial virus-associated acute encephalopathy. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 劳伦凤蝶(Papiliotrema laurentii)是一种环境酵母,越来越多地被认为是免疫功能低下个体侵袭性感染的原因,但日本的报道有限。该研究需要记录一名因 呼吸道合胞病毒 相关急性脑病而接受甲泼尼龙冲击治疗的儿童发生劳伦凤蝶血流感染的罕见病例。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一名患有脑瘫和癫痫的 4 岁日本女孩 病例报告 的单例患者,她在接受 呼吸道合胞病毒 相关急性脑病的甲泼尼龙冲击治疗后出现劳伦凤蝶真菌血症。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基质辅助激光解吸/电离飞行时间质谱法以及内部转录间隔区和 D1/D2 区域的测序来鉴定分离物。进行抗真菌药敏试验,根据药敏结果将治疗由米卡芬净调整为脂质体两性霉素B,随后调整为氟康唑。
elements_zh.main_results: 完成 3 天类固醇治疗后 3 天进行的血培养显示出酵母样生物,后来证实为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌敏感性测试显示出与普通酵母不同的特征。患者在 6 个月的随访中完全康复并保持无复发。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这是日本首例报告的劳氏凤蝶真菌血症病例,凸显了甲基泼尼松龙脉冲疗法甚至可能使免疫功能正常的儿童易患机会性真菌血症。准确的鉴定和药敏测试对于适当的抗真菌管理至关重要。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了在接受免疫抑制治疗的儿童中需要提高对罕见真菌病原体的临床认识,以及指导抗真菌药物 治疗 的精确诊断方法的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这限制了普遍性并排除了因果推断。诊断局限性和漏报可能导致低估 Papiliotrema laurentii 发病率,需要提高 监测 和诊断能力。

abstract_zh: 劳伦凤蝶是一种环境酵母菌,越来越多地被认为是侵袭性感染的原因,特别是在细胞免疫受损的个体中。然而,日本的报道有限。我们描述了一名患有脑瘫和癫痫的 4 岁日本女孩,由劳伦凤蝶引起的血流感染的罕见病例。她被诊断患有呼吸道合胞病毒相关急性脑病,并接受甲泼尼龙冲击治疗作为强化治疗的一部分尽管完成了 3 天的类固醇治疗,她的发烧仍然持续。类固醇治疗完成 3 天后进行的后续血培养显示存在酵母样生物体。使用基质辅助激光解吸/电离飞行时间质谱和内部转录间隔区和 D1/D2 区域的测序,将该分离株鉴定为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌药敏测试显示其特征谱与常见的不同。米卡芬净改用脂质体两性霉素 B,后来改用氟康唑,病情完全缓解。6 个月随访后,患者未复发。据我们所知,这是日本首例报道的凤蝶真菌血症病例;然而,由于诊断局限性和有限的 发病率 数据,其真实的 发病率 可能被低估。该病例表明,甲泼尼龙冲击治疗甚至可能使免疫功能正常的儿童易患机会性真菌血症,准确的识别和药敏测试对于适当的抗真菌治疗至关重要。
summary_zh: 劳伦凤蝶是一种环境酵母菌,越来越多地被认为是侵袭性感染的原因,特别是在细胞免疫受损的个体中。然而,日本的报道有限。我们描述了一名患有脑瘫和癫痫的 4 岁日本女孩,由劳伦凤蝶引起的血流感染的罕见病例。她被诊断患有呼吸道合胞病毒相关急性脑病,并接受甲泼尼龙冲击治疗作为强化治疗的一部分尽管完成了 3 天的类固醇治疗,她的发烧仍然持续。类固醇治疗完成 3 天后进行的后续血培养显示存在酵母样生物体。使用基质辅助激光解吸/电离飞行时间质谱和内部转录间隔区和 D1/D2 区域的测序,将该分离株鉴定为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌药敏测试显示其特征谱与常见的不同。米卡芬净改用脂质体两性霉素 B,后来改用氟康唑,病情完全缓解。6 个月随访后,患者未复发。据我们所知,这是日本首例报道的凤蝶真菌血症病例;然而,由于诊断局限性和有限的 发病率 数据,其真实的 发病率 可能被低估。该病例表明,甲泼尼龙冲击治疗甚至可能使免疫功能正常的儿童易患机会性真菌血症,准确的识别和药敏测试对于适当的抗真菌治疗至关重要。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 劳伦凤蝶(Papiliotrema laurentii)是一种环境酵母,越来越多地被认为是免疫功能低下个体侵袭性感染的原因,但日本的报道有限。该研究需要记录一名因 呼吸道合胞病毒 相关急性脑病而接受甲泼尼龙冲击治疗的儿童发生劳伦凤蝶血流感染的罕见病例。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一名患有脑瘫和癫痫的 4 岁日本女孩 病例报告 的单例患者,她在接受 呼吸道合胞病毒 相关急性脑病的甲泼尼龙冲击治疗后出现劳伦凤蝶真菌血症。
analysis_zh.methods: 使用基质辅助激光解吸/电离飞行时间质谱法以及内部转录间隔区和 D1/D2 区域的测序来鉴定分离物。进行抗真菌药敏试验,根据药敏结果将治疗由米卡芬净调整为脂质体两性霉素B,随后调整为氟康唑。
analysis_zh.main_results: 完成 3 天类固醇治疗后 3 天进行的血培养显示出酵母样生物,后来证实为 Papiliotrema laurentii。抗真菌敏感性测试显示出与普通酵母不同的特征。患者在 6 个月的随访中完全康复并保持无复发。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这是日本首例报告的劳氏凤蝶真菌血症病例,凸显了甲基泼尼松龙脉冲疗法甚至可能使免疫功能正常的儿童易患机会性真菌血症。准确的鉴定和药敏测试对于适当的抗真菌管理至关重要。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该病例强调了在接受免疫抑制治疗的儿童中需要提高对罕见真菌病原体的临床认识,以及指导抗真菌药物 治疗 的精确诊断方法的重要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于单个 病例报告,这限制了普遍性并排除了因果推断。诊断局限性和漏报可能导致低估 Papiliotrema laurentii 发病率,需要提高 监测 和诊断能力。

title: Respiratory viruses in bronchoalveolar lavage: A Retrospective study of clinical and laboratory features in immunocompromised children
abstract: Background Immunocompromised children are at high risk for pulmonary infections caused by a broad spectrum of pathogens. Although bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) combined with multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) facilitates detection of respiratory viruses in the lower respiratory tract, pediatric data remain limited. Objectives To determine the prevalence of respiratory viruses detected in BAL fluid and to describe the associated clinical, radiologic, and laboratory characteristics in immunocompromised children. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study of immunocompromised patients aged 1–20 years who underwent flexible bronchoscopy with BAL for evaluation of new pulmonary infiltrates at a tertiary care center between January 2016 and June 2025. Respiratory viruses were identified using multiplex real-time PCR. Patients were categorized into virus-positive and virus-negative groups for comparative analysis. Results Among 94 patients included in the analysis, respiratory viruses were detected in 27 cases (28.7%). Rhino/Enterovirus was the predominant pathogen (59.2%), followed by adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and bocavirus. Patients in the virus-positive group were more likely to receive trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis (96.3% vs 71.6%, p = 0.010). Clinical features including cough (74.1% vs 40.3%, p = 0.003), sputum production (61.5% vs 29.9%, p = 0.005), and crepitations on chest examination (37.0% vs 13.4%, p = 0.010) were significantly more common in the virus-positive group. However, chest radiographic and computed tomography findings did not differ significantly between groups. Clinical outcomes, including pediatric intensive care unit admission, respiratory failure, and length of hospital stay, were also comparable. BAL galactomannan positivity was more frequent in virus-positive patients (50.0% vs 15.6%, p = 0.005), suggesting possible fungal co-infection. Conclusions Respiratory viruses are frequently detected in BAL fluid from immunocompromised children with pulmonary infiltrates, with Rhino/Enterovirus being the predominant virus identified. Patients with viral detection were more likely to receive trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis and to present with cough, sputum production, and crepitations on chest examination. Radiologic features and clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between virus-positive and virus-negative groups. The higher prevalence of BAL galactomannan positivity in virus-positive patients raises the possibility of fungal co-infection.

Introduction Immunocompromised children are at significantly increased risk for pulmonary infections because of impaired host immune defenses, with respiratory viral infections contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality in this population [1]. Pulmonary infiltrates in these patients may result from opportunistic infections, including bacterial, viral, or fungal pathogens, as well as non-infectious conditions such as pulmonary hemorrhage, fluid overload, or malignancy. Differentiating among these etiologies remains clinically challenging because clinical manifestations and radiologic findings on chest radiographs or computed tomography (CT) often lack specificity, particularly in children. Flexible bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a valuable and relatively safe diagnostic procedure for identifying pathogens responsible for lower respiratory tract infections and other pulmonary diseases [1, 2]. The implementation of multiplex viral polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays on BAL specimens has substantially improved the detection of respiratory viruses in immunocompromised patients, increasing diagnostic yield up to 25% compared with conventional viral culture methods (6%) [3]. Previous studies in hospitalized adults demonstrated that PCR detected viral nucleic acid in 17.4% (91/522) of BAL specimens, predominantly among transplant recipients and other immunocompromised hosts [4]. In that cohort, coronaviruses were the most frequently detected viruses (32.3%), followed by rhinoviruses (22.6%) and parainfluenza viruses (19.5%) [4]. Respiratory viral detection was independently associated with poor response to antibiotics and absence of radiologic infiltrates [4]. In immunocompromised adults, the diagnostic yield of BAL ranges from 26% to 69% [5]. Similarly, studies in immunocompromised children have reported variable diagnostic yields ranging from 28% to 68% [6, 7]. Nadimpalli et al. [7] reported an overall diagnostic yield of 31% in a 10-year review involving 123 immunocompromised children. Importantly, the clinical utility of BAL extends beyond pathogen identification, as BAL findings—whether positive or negative—have been shown to alter or narrow antimicrobial therapy in approximately 50%–53% of pediatric cases [6]. At our hospital, multiplex PCR assays for respiratory viral detection in BAL fluid have been routinely implemented since 2016. However, pediatric data regarding respiratory viral detection in BAL specimens remain limited, particularly in immunocompromised children. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of respiratory viruses detected in BAL fluid and to evaluate the associated clinical Page 3/22 characteristics, diagnostic yield, and impact on management and outcomes in immunocompromised children with pulmonary infiltrates at a tertiary care university hospital. Materials and Methods Study Population This retrospective observational study included immunocompromised children aged 1–20 years who underwent flexible bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) at tertiary care hospital between January 2016 and June 2025. Patients were identified from an institutional bronchoscopy database, and clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. The study protocol was approved by the Human Research Ethics Committee (Approval No. MURA2025/578). Patients were classified as immunocompromised if they had undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) or solid organ transplantation, had hematologic malignancy or non-malignant hematologic disease, solid tumors receiving chemotherapy, primary immunodeficiency, or were receiving immunosuppressive medications. Eligible patients were required to have newly developed pulmonary infiltrates identified on chest radiography or computed tomography (CT). Patients with incomplete medical records were excluded from the analysis. Demographic and clinical data were collected, including age, sex, underlying immunocompromised conditions, prior hospitalization before bronchoscopy, and use of immunosuppressive medications, systemic corticosteroids, chemotherapy, antimicrobial agents, antifungal agents, and trimethoprim- sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis within 30 days prior to assessment. Clinical presentations documented within 7 days before bronchoscopy included fever, maximum body temperature, cough, sputum production and its characteristics, rhinorrhea and its characteristics, dyspnea, and respiratory support requirements prior to bronchoscopy, including oxygen supplementation, high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), and mechanical ventilatory support. Physical examination findings included abnormal lung auscultation, rhonchi, wheezing, crepitations, and decreased breath sounds. Radiologic findings from chest radiographs and CT scans were reviewed, including pulmonary opacities, bilateral infiltrates, air bronchograms, consolidation, nodules, ground-glass opacities, reticular infiltrations, tree-in-bud pattern, pleural effusion, and atelectasis. Laboratory investigations included complete blood counts obtained prior to bronchoscopy, absolute neutrophil and lymphocyte counts, BAL differential cell counts, BAL galactomannan assay, potassium hydroxide (KOH) preparation, cytomegalovirus (CMV) testing, bacterial cultures, and multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) respiratory viral panels performed on BAL fluid using either 23- or 33- pathogen panels. Page 4/22 Respiratory viruses detected from BAL fluid were classified as virus-positive pneumonia, whereas patients without viral detection were categorized as the non-viral pneumonia group. Secondary clinical outcomes included pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission, maximum required respiratory support, severe respiratory failure, and length of hospital stay. Statistical Analysis Statistical analyses were performed using Stata version 19.0 (StataCorp, College Station, TX, USA). Continuous variables were expressed as medians with interquartile ranges (IQRs), whereas categorical variables were presented as frequencies and percentages. Comparisons between virus-positive and non- viral groups were performed using Student’s t-test or the Mann–Whitney U test for continuous variables, and the chi-square test or Fisher’s exact test for categorical variables, as appropriate. Univariable logistic regression analysis was initially performed to identify factors associated with respiratory viral detection in BAL fluid. Variables with statistical significance or clinical relevance in the univariable analysis were subsequently included in the multivariable logistic regression model to determine independent predictors of viral pneumonia. Crude and adjusted odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were reported. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was performed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of the multivariable predictive model for viral pneumonia. A two-sided p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results A total of 197 immunocompromised pediatric patients who underwent bronchoscopy were initially identified; 103 patients were excluded, including 64 whose medical records could not be obtained and 39 who did not undergo multiplex PCR respiratory virus panel testing. Consequently, 94 patients who underwent 23- or 33-pathogen respiratory virus panel testing using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) were included in the final analysis. Among them, respiratory viruses were detected in BAL fluid from 27 patients (28.7%), whereas 67 patients (71.3%) had no viral detection. As shown in Table 1, Rhino/Enterovirus was the predominant pathogen, accounting for 59.2% of virus- positive cases, followed by adenovirus, human metapneumovirus (hMPV), and bocavirus (7.4% each). Other detected viruses included parainfluenza virus types 3 and 4, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), coronavirus NL63, and coronavirus 229E. Read Full License Additional Declarations: No competing interests reported. Page 1/22 Abstract Background Immunocompromised children are at high risk for pulmonary infections caused by a broad spectrum of pathogens. Although bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) combined with multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) facilitates detection of respiratory viruses in the lower respiratory tract, pediatric data remain limited. Objectives To determine the prevalence of respiratory viruses detected in BAL fluid and to describe the associated clinical, radiologic, and laboratory characteristics in immunocompromised children. Methods We conducted a retrospective observational study of immunocompromised patients aged 1–20 years who underwent flexible bronchoscopy with BAL for evaluation of new pulmonary infiltrates at a tertiary care center between January 2016 and June 2025. Respiratory viruses were identified using multiplex real-time PCR. Patients were categorized into virus-positive and virus-negative groups for comparative analysis. Results Among 94 patients included in the analysis, respiratory viruses were detected in 27 cases (28.7%). Rhino/Enterovirus was the predominant pathogen (59.2%), followed by adenovirus, human metapneumovirus, and bocavirus. Patients in the virus-positive group were more likely to receive trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis (96.3% vs 71.6%, p = 0.010). Clinical features including cough (74.1% vs 40.3%, p = 0.003), sputum production (61.5% vs 29.9%, p = 0.005), and crepitations on chest examination (37.0% vs 13.4%, p = 0.010) were significantly more common in the virus-positive group. However, chest radiographic and computed tomography findings did not differ significantly between groups. Clinical outcomes, including pediatric intensive care unit admission, respiratory failure, and length of hospital stay, were also comparable. BAL galactomannan positivity was more frequent in virus-positive patients (50.0% vs 15.6%, p = 0.005), suggesting possible fungal co- infection. Conclusions Page 2/22 Respiratory viruses are frequently detected in BAL fluid from immunocompromised children with pulmonary infiltrates, with Rhino/Enterovirus being the predominant virus identified. Patients with viral detection were more likely to receive trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole prophylaxis and to present with cough, sputum production, and crepitations on chest examination. Radiologic features and clinical outcomes did not differ significantly between virus-positive and virus-negative groups. The higher prevalence of BAL galactomannan positivity in virus-positive patients raises the possibility of fungal co- infection. Introduction Immunocompromised children are at significantly increased risk for pulmonary infections because of impaired host immune defenses, with respiratory viral infections contributing substantially to morbidity and mortality in this population [1]. Pulmonary infiltrates in these patients may result from opportunistic infections, including bacterial, viral, or fungal pathogens, as well as non-infectious conditions such as pulmonary hemorrhage, fluid overload, or malignancy. Differentiating among these etiologies remains clinically challenging because clinical manifestations and radiologic findings on chest radiographs or computed tomography (CT) often lack specificity, particularly in children. Flexible bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is a valuable and relatively safe diagnostic procedure for identifying pathogens responsible for lower respiratory tract infections and other pulmonary diseases [1, 2]. The implementation of multiplex viral polymerase chain reaction (PCR) assays on BAL specimens has substantially improved the detection of respiratory viruses in immunocompromised patients, increasing diagnostic yield up to 25% compared with conventional viral culture methods (6%) [3]. Previous studies in hospitalized adults demonstrated that PCR detected viral nucleic acid in 17.4% (91/522) of BAL specimens, predominantly among transplant recipients and other immunocompromised hosts [4]. In that cohort, coronaviruses were the most frequently detected viruses (32.3%), followed by rhinoviruses (22.6%) and parainfluenza viruses (19.5%) [4]. Respiratory viral detection was independently associated with poor response to antibiotics and absence of radiologic infiltrates [4]. In immunocompromised adults, the diagnostic yield of BAL ranges from 26% to 69% [5]. Similarly, studies in immunocompromised children have reported variable diagnostic yields ranging from 28% to 68% [6, 7]. Nadimpalli et al. [7] reported an overall diagnostic yield of 31% in a 10-year review involving 123 immunocompromised children. Importantly, the clinical utility of BAL extends beyond pathogen identification, as BAL findings—whether positive or negative—have been shown to alter or narrow antimicrobial therapy in approximately 50%–53% of pediatric cases [6]. At our hospital, multiplex PCR assays for respiratory viral detection in BAL fluid have been routinely implemented since 2016. However, pediatric data regarding respiratory viral detection in BAL specimens remain limited, particularly in immunocompromised children. This study aimed to determine the prevalence of respiratory viruses detected in BAL fluid and to evaluate the associated clinical Page 3/22 characteristics, diagnostic yield, and impact on management and outcomes in immunocompromised children with pulmonary infiltrates at a tertiary care university hospital. Materials and Methods Study Population This retrospective observational study included immunocompromised children aged 1–20 years who underwent flexible bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) at tertiary care hospital between January 2016 and June 2025. Patients were identified from an institutional bronchoscopy database, and clinical data were extracted from electronic medical records. The study protocol was approved by the Human Research Ethics Committee (Approval No. MURA2025/578). Patients were classified as immunocompromised if they had undergone hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) or solid organ transplantation, had hematologic malignancy or non-malignant hematologic disease, solid tumors receiving chemotherapy, primary immunodeficiency, or were receiving immunosuppressive medications. Eligible patients were required to have newly developed pulmonary infiltrates identified on chest radiography or computed tomography (CT). Patients with incomplete medical records were excluded from the analysis. Demographic and clinical data were collected, including age, sex, underlying immunocompromised conditions, prior hospitalization before bronchoscopy, and use of immunosuppressive medications, systemic corticosteroids, chemotherapy, antimicrobial agents, antifungal agents, and trimethoprim- sulfamethoxazole (Bactrim) prophylaxis within 30 days prior to assessment. Clinical presentations documented within 7 days before bronchoscopy included fever, maximum body temperature, cough, sputum production and its characteristics, rhinorrhea and its characteristics, dyspnea, and respiratory support requirements prior to bronchoscopy, including oxygen supplementation, high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC), and mechanical ventilatory support. full_text: The Journal for Translational Respiratory Immunology is a rigorous, peer-reviewed scientific journal dedicated to publishing high-impact research at the critical intersection of the respiratory system and immune defense mechanisms. Our mission is to accelerate the translation of basic scientific discoveries into actionable clinical practice, bridging the gap between laboratory research (bench) and patient care (bedside) to ultimately improve global respiratory health. The journal provides a dynamic and comprehensive platform for researchers, clinicians, and academicians to share novel insights, experimental findings, and clinical trials. We focus on the complex biological mechanisms by which immunological and virological factors influence respiratory health and drive the pathogenesis of pulmonary diseases. The journal is committed to advancing medical science by fostering interdisciplinary collaboration among specialists in respiratory care, virology, and immunopathology. Key Subject Areas We welcome original research articles, comprehensive reviews, clinical trials, and case studies across the following core disciplines: - Respiratory Medicine: Research detailing the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and innovative treatments of acute and chronic airway diseases, including asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), cystic fibrosis, and interstitial lung diseases. - Immunology: Investigations into the innate and adaptive immune responses within the respiratory mucosa, host-pathogen interactions, allergic responses, immunodeficiencies, and the development of targeted immunotherapeutics. - Virology: Studies focusing on the pathogenesis, epidemiology, and molecular biology of respiratory viral infections (such as Influenza, RSV, and emerging Coronaviruses), as well as vaccine efficacy and novel antiviral strategies. - Pulmonary Medicine: Clinical advancements in the management of complex pulmonary disorders, intensive care respiratory interventions, pulmonary hemodynamics, and advanced diagnostic modalities.
